title.zh: 卷四百二十七 列傳第一百八十六 道學一 周敦頤 程顥 程頤 張載弟:戩 邵雍
title.en: Volume 427 Biographies 186: Taoist Scholars 1 - Zhou Dunyi, Cheng Hao, Cheng Yi, Zhang Zai and younger brother: Jian, Shao Yong
title.raw: 卷四百二十七 列傳第一百八十六 道學一 周敦頤 程顥 程頤 張載弟:戩 邵雍 Volume 427 Biographies 186: Taoist Scholars 1 - Zhou Dunyi, Cheng Hao, Cheng Yi, Zhang Zai and younger brother: Jian, Shao Yong

sentences.zh: 周敦頤 程顥 程頤 張載弟:戩 邵雍

translations.literal: Zhou Dunyi, Cheng Hao, Cheng Yi, Zhang Zai's younger brother Jian, Shao Yong
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dunyi; Cheng Hao; Cheng Yi; Zhang Zai and his younger brother Jian; Shao Yong

sentences.zh: 「道學」之名，古無是也。

translations.literal: The name "Learning of the Way"—in antiquity there was no such thing.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times there was no such term as "Learning of the Way."

sentences.zh: 三代盛時，天子以是道為政教，大臣百官有司以是道為職業，黨、庠、術、序師弟子以是道為講習，四方百姓日用是道而不知。

translations.literal: In the flourishing age of the Three Dynasties, the Son of Heaven took this Way as governance and teaching, great ministers, officials, and clerks took this Way as their occupation, in party halls, village schools, and state academies teachers and pupils took this Way for study and practice, and the people in all directions daily used this Way without knowing it.
translations.idiomatic: In the golden age of the Three Dynasties, the Son of Heaven made this Way the foundation of government and education; ministers, officials, and clerks made it their professional duty; in local schools and state academies, teachers and pupils made it the subject of study; and ordinary people throughout the realm lived by it every day without even being aware of it.

sentences.zh: 是故盈覆載之間，無一民一物不被是道之澤，以遂其性。

translations.literal: Therefore, within what fills and covers and bears all, not one person or thing failed to receive the grace of this Way, so as to fulfill their natures.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, throughout all that heaven covers and earth bears, there was not a single person or thing that did not enjoy the bounty of this Way and thereby fulfill its proper nature.

sentences.zh: 于斯時也，道學之名，何自而立哉。

translations.literal: At such a time, by what could the name "Learning of the Way" have arisen and been established?
translations.idiomatic: At such a time, what need could there have been for a separate name called "Learning of the Way"?

sentences.zh: 文王、周公既沒，孔子有德無位，既不能使是道之用漸被斯世，退而與其徒定禮樂，明憲章，刪《詩》，修《春秋》，贊《易象》，討論《墳》、《典》，期使五三聖人之道昭明於無窮。

translations.literal: After King Wen and the Duke of Zhou had passed away, Confucius had virtue but no position; being unable to cause the application of this Way gradually to spread over this age, he withdrew and with his disciples fixed ritual and music, clarified statutes and regulations, edited the Odes, revised the Spring and Autumn Annals, assisted the Images of the Changes, and discussed the Documents and Canon, hoping to make the Way of the Five and Three Sages brilliantly clear to infinity.
translations.idiomatic: After King Wen and the Duke of Zhou died, Confucius possessed virtue but held no office. Unable to see this Way gradually applied throughout the world, he withdrew and, with his disciples, established ritual and music, clarified laws and institutions, edited the Odes, revised the Spring and Autumn Annals, elucidated the Images of the Changes, and studied the ancient documents, aiming to keep the Way of the sages of the Three Dynasties and the Five Emperors shining forth without end.

sentences.zh: 故曰：「夫子賢于堯、舜遠矣。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: "The Master is far more worthy than Yao and Shun."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "The Master surpasses Yao and Shun by far."

sentences.zh: 」孔子沒，曾子獨得其傳，傳之子思，以及孟子，孟子沒而無傳。

translations.literal: When Confucius died, Zengzi alone received its transmission; he transmitted it to Zisi, and on to Mencius; when Mencius died, there was no transmission.
translations.idiomatic: When Confucius died, only Zengzi received the full transmission. He passed it to Zisi, and then to Mencius; after Mencius died, the line was broken.

sentences.zh: 兩漢而下，儒者之論大道，察焉而弗精，語焉而弗詳，異端邪說起而乘之，幾至大壞。

translations.literal: From the Two Han dynasties downward, when Confucians discussed the Great Way, they perceived it but were not precise, spoke of it but were not thorough; heterodox and perverse doctrines arose and took advantage, nearly bringing great ruin.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han dynasties onward, when Confucian scholars discussed the Great Way, their grasp was inexact and their exposition incomplete. Heterodox teachings arose to exploit the confusion, and the tradition came close to utter ruin.

sentences.zh: 千有餘載，至宋中葉，周敦頤出於舂陵，乃得聖賢不傳之學，作《太極圖說》、《通書》，推明陰陽五行之理，命於天而性於人者，了若指掌。

translations.literal: After more than a thousand years, reaching the middle of the Song, Zhou Dunyi came forth from Chunling and obtained the learning of the sages and worthies that had not been transmitted; he composed Explanations of the Diagram of the Supreme Pole and Penetrating the Book, extending and clarifying the principles of yin and yang and the five phases; what is mandated by Heaven and what is nature in man became as clear as pointing at the palm.
translations.idiomatic: More than a millennium later, in the mid-Song period, Zhou Dunyi of Chunling recovered the sage learning that had ceased to be transmitted. In his Explanations of the Diagram of the Supreme Pole and Penetrating the Book, he elucidated the principles of yin and yang and the five phases so that what Heaven mandates and what constitutes human nature became as plain as the lines on one's palm.

sentences.zh: 張載作《西銘》，又極言理一分殊之旨，然後道之大原出於天者，灼然而無疑焉。

translations.literal: Zhang Zai composed the Western Inscription, and further expounded to the utmost the purport that principle is one yet its manifestations are many; thereafter the great origin of the Way that issues from Heaven became blazingly clear and beyond doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zai wrote the Western Inscription and developed at length the doctrine that principle is one while its particular manifestations are many. Thereafter the great source of the Way, which issues from Heaven, stood forth brilliantly and beyond dispute.

sentences.zh: 仁宗明道初年，程顥及弟頤實生，及長，受業周氏，已乃擴大其所聞，表章《大學》、《中庸》二篇，與《語》、《孟》並行，於是上自帝王傅心之奧，下至初學入德之門。

translations.literal: In the early years of the Mingdao reign of Emperor Renzong, Cheng Hao and his younger brother Yi were actually born; when grown, they received instruction from the Zhou school, and thereafter enlarged what they had heard, giving prominence to the two chapters Great Learning and Doctrine of the Mean, setting them alongside the Analects and Mencius, so that from above, the subtlety by which emperors transmit the heart, down to below, the gate by which beginners enter virtue—
translations.idiomatic: In the early Mingdao era of Emperor Renzong, Cheng Hao and his younger brother Yi were born. When they came of age they studied under Zhou Dunyi, then expanded on what they had learned. They gave special prominence to the Great Learning and the Doctrine of the Mean, placing them alongside the Analects and Mencius, so that everything from the subtle art by which rulers transmit the mind-and-heart down to the gateway through which beginners enter the path of virtue—

sentences.zh: 融會貫通，無復餘蘊。

translations.literal: was fused and penetrated through, with no remainder of meaning left unrevealed.
translations.idiomatic: was brought into a single coherent whole, with nothing left unexplained.

sentences.zh: 迄宋南渡，新安朱熹得程氏正傳，其學加親切焉。

translations.literal: Reaching the Song's crossing south of the Yangzi, Zhu Xi of Xin'an received the true transmission of the Cheng school, and his learning became yet more intimate and immediate.
translations.idiomatic: After the Song court moved south across the Yangzi, Zhu Xi of Xin'an received the authentic transmission of the Cheng school and carried the learning to an even greater depth of personal engagement.

sentences.zh: 大抵以格物致知為先，明善誠身為要，凡《詩》、《書》，六藝之文，與夫孔、孟之遺言，顛錯于秦火，支離於漢儒，幽沉于魏、晉六朝者，至是皆煥然而大明，秩然而各得其所。

translations.literal: Generally taking investigation of things and extension of knowledge as primary, and clarifying goodness and making the self sincere as essential, all the texts of the Odes, Documents, and the Six Arts, together with the surviving words of Confucius and Mencius that had been overturned and confused by the Qin burning, fragmented by Han Confucians, and sunk in obscurity through Wei, Jin, and the Six Dynasties—at this time all became brilliantly clear, orderly, and each restored to its proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Taking investigation of things and extension of knowledge as the starting point and clarifying goodness and making the self sincere as the essential aim, he restored to clarity all the texts of the classics and the Six Arts, together with the teachings of Confucius and Mencius that had been scattered by the Qin bibliocaust, fragmented by Han commentators, and buried in obscurity through Wei, Jin, and the Six Dynasties. At last they shone forth in full light, each in its proper order and place.

sentences.zh: 此宋儒之學所以度越諸子，而上接孟氏者歟。

translations.literal: Is this not why the learning of Song Confucians surpassed the various masters and connected upward with Mencius?
translations.idiomatic: This is why the learning of the Song Confucians surpassed all earlier schools and reconnected with Mencius.

sentences.zh: 其于世代之汙隆，氣化之榮悴，有所關係也甚大。

translations.literal: Its relation to the rise and fall of ages and the flourishing and withering of cosmic transformation is very great indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Its bearing on the rise and decline of dynasties and the flourishing and decay of civilizations was profound indeed.

sentences.zh: 道學盛于宋，宋弗究於用，甚至有厲禁焉。

translations.literal: Learning of the Way flourished in the Song, yet the Song did not fully apply it in practice; there were even severe prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of the Way reached its height under the Song, yet the Song never fully put it into practice—indeed, there were times when it was harshly suppressed.

sentences.zh: 後之時君世主，欲復天德王道之治，必來此取法矣。

translations.literal: Later rulers and lords of the age who wish to restore the governance of Heaven's virtue and the kingly Way must come here to take their model.
translations.idiomatic: Future rulers who wish to restore the governance of Heaven's virtue and the kingly Way will have to look to this tradition for their model.

sentences.zh: 邵雍高明英悟，程氏實推重之，舊史列之隱逸，未當，今置張載後。

translations.literal: Shao Yong was lofty, bright, and penetratingly intelligent; the Cheng brothers truly held him in high esteem. The old histories listed him among recluses, which was inappropriate; now he is placed after Zhang Zai.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Yong was exceptionally brilliant and perceptive, and the Cheng brothers genuinely held him in the highest regard. Earlier histories wrongly classified him among recluses; here he is placed after Zhang Zai.

sentences.zh: 張栻之學，亦出程氏，既見朱熹，相與博約又大進焉。

translations.literal: Zhang Shi's learning also issued from the Cheng school; after he met Zhu Xi, through mutual broadening and narrowing their understanding advanced greatly again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi's learning likewise derived from the Cheng school. After he met Zhu Xi, their exchanges led to a great further advance in both men's understanding.

sentences.zh: 其他程、朱門人，考其源委，各以類從，作《道學傳》。

translations.literal: As for other disciples of the Cheng and Zhu schools, tracing their origins and branches, each is grouped by category, composing the Biographies of Learning of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Other disciples of the Cheng and Zhu schools are traced to their sources and grouped by lineage in the Biographies of Learning of the Way.

sentences.zh: 周敦頤

translations.literal: Zhou Dunyi
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dunyi

sentences.zh: 周敦頤，字茂叔，道州營道人。

translations.literal: Zhou Dunyi, courtesy name Maoshu, was a native of Yingdao in Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dunyi, styled Maoshu, was a native of Yingdao in Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 元名敦實，避英宗舊諱改焉。

translations.literal: His original name was Dunshi; he changed it to avoid the taboo name of the former emperor Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: His original given name was Dunshi; he changed it to avoid the taboo on the former Emperor Yingzong's name.

sentences.zh: 以舅龍圖閣學士鄭向任，為分寧主簿。

translations.literal: Through his maternal uncle Zheng Xiang, Academician of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams, he obtained an appointment and served as chief clerk of Fenning.
translations.idiomatic: Through the patronage of his maternal uncle Zheng Xiang, Academician of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams, he was appointed chief clerk of Fenning County.

sentences.zh: 有獄久不決，敦頤至，一訊立辨。

translations.literal: There was a case long unresolved; when Dunyi arrived, one interrogation immediately settled it.
translations.idiomatic: A lawsuit had long gone unresolved; when Dunyi arrived, a single hearing settled the matter at once.

sentences.zh: 邑人驚曰：「老吏不如也。

translations.literal: The townspeople exclaimed in amazement: "The old clerks are not his equal."
translations.idiomatic: The townspeople marveled: "Even our veteran clerks are no match for him."

sentences.zh: 」部使者薦之，調南安軍司理參軍。

translations.literal: The circuit intendant recommended him, and he was transferred to serve as judicial assistant in Nan'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit intendant recommended him, and he was transferred to the post of judicial assistant in Nan'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有囚法不當死，轉運使王逵欲深治之。

translations.literal: There was a prisoner whom the law did not require to die, but the transport commissioner Wang Kui wished to punish him severely.
translations.idiomatic: A prisoner whose offense did not warrant death faced prosecution by Transport Commissioner Wang Kui, who sought the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 逵，酷悍吏也，眾莫敢爭，敦頤獨與之辨，不聽，乃委手版歸，將棄官去，曰：「如此尚可仕乎！

translations.literal: Kui was a cruel and fierce official; none dared dispute with him. Dunyi alone argued with him; when Kui would not listen, Dunyi laid down his official tablet and returned home, about to abandon his post and leave, saying: "How can one still serve in office under such conditions!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kui was a cruel and overbearing official, and no one dared oppose him. Dunyi alone argued the case. When Kui refused to listen, Dunyi resigned his commission and prepared to leave office, saying, "How can one continue to serve under such circumstances!"

sentences.zh: 殺人以媚人，吾不為也。

translations.literal: To kill a man in order to please another—I will not do it.
translations.idiomatic: I will not take a man's life merely to curry favor with my superiors."

sentences.zh: 」逵悟，囚得免。

translations.literal: Kui came to his senses, and the prisoner was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kui came to his senses, and the prisoner was spared.

sentences.zh: 移郴之桂陽令，治績尤著。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be magistrate of Guiyang in Chen prefecture, where his administrative achievements were especially notable.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Guiyang in Chen Prefecture, where his administrative achievements were especially distinguished.

sentences.zh: 郡守李初平賢之，語之曰：「吾欲讀書，何如？

translations.literal: The prefect Li Chuping regarded him as worthy and said to him: "I wish to study books—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Li Chuping admired him and said, "I would like to take up serious study—what do you advise?"

sentences.zh: 」敦頤曰：「公老無及矣，請為公言之。

translations.literal: Dunyi said: "Your Excellency is old and it is too late to catch up, but please allow me to explain for you."
translations.idiomatic: Dunyi replied, "Your Excellency is too advanced in years to master everything, but let me explain the essentials for you."

sentences.zh: 」二年果有得。

translations.literal: After two years he indeed made gains.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years the prefect had genuinely made progress.

sentences.zh: 徙知南昌，南昌人皆曰：「是能辨分寧獄者，吾屬得所訴矣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administer Nanchang; the people of Nanchang all said: "This is the one who could settle the Fenning lawsuit—we have found someone to whom we can bring our grievances."
translations.idiomatic: When he was appointed prefect of Nanchang, the people said, "This is the man who settled the Fenning case at a single hearing—we finally have someone to whom we can bring our grievances."

sentences.zh: 」富家大姓、黠吏惡少，惴惴焉不獨以得罪於令為憂，而又以污穢善政為恥。

translations.literal: Wealthy great clans, cunning clerks, and wicked young men trembled with fear—not only worrying about offending the magistrate, but also ashamed to defile good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy clans, crafty clerks, and local bullies trembled with apprehension—not only for fear of offending the magistrate, but also because they were ashamed to stain his good administration with their misconduct.

sentences.zh: 曆合州判官，事不經手，吏不敢決。

translations.literal: He served successively as assistant prefect of Hezhou; matters did not pass through his hands, and the clerks dared not decide them.
translations.idiomatic: As assistant prefect of Hezhou, he refused to sign off on cases he had not personally examined, and the clerks dared not decide matters on their own.

sentences.zh: 雖下之，民不肯從。

translations.literal: Even when orders were issued, the people would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Even when official orders were issued, the people refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 部使者趙抃惑於譖口，臨之甚威，敦頤處之超然。

translations.literal: The circuit intendant Zhao Bian was misled by slanderous words and treated him with great severity; Dunyi bore it with complete detachment.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit Intendant Zhao Bian, misled by slander, treated him with great harshness, but Dunyi remained utterly unperturbed.

sentences.zh: 通判虔州，抃守虔，熟視其所為，乃大悟，執其手曰：「吾幾失君矣，今而後乃知周茂叔也。」

translations.literal: As vice-prefect of Qianzhou, Bian was prefect of Qian; after closely observing his conduct, he came to a great awakening, took his hand and said: "I nearly lost you! Only now do I truly know Zhou Maoshu."
translations.idiomatic: When Dunyi served as vice-prefect of Qianzhou under Prefect Zhao Bian, Bian closely observed his conduct and came to a full realization of his character. Taking his hand, he said, "I nearly lost a man of your caliber. Only now do I truly know Zhou Maoshu."

sentences.zh: 熙甯初，知郴州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xining era, he was appointed prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xining era, he was appointed prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 用抃及呂公著薦，為廣東轉運判官，提點刑獄，以洗冤澤物為己任。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Bian and Lü Gongzhu, he became transport vice-commissioner of Guangdong and judicial intendant, taking the clearing of wrongful convictions and the benefiting of things as his personal charge.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Zhao Bian and Lü Gongzhu, he was appointed transport vice-commissioner of Guangdong and judicial intendant, making the redress of wrongful convictions and the welfare of the people his personal mission.

sentences.zh: 行部不憚勞苦，雖瘴癘險遠，亦緩視徐按。

translations.literal: On inspection tours he did not fear hardship; even in malarial and dangerous remote regions, he proceeded slowly and examined matters carefully.
translations.idiomatic: On his inspection tours he shrank from no hardship; even in malarial and remote districts he proceeded deliberately and examined every case with care.

sentences.zh: 以疾求知南康軍。

translations.literal: Because of illness he requested appointment to Nancong Army.
translations.idiomatic: Illness led him to request appointment as prefect of Nancong.

sentences.zh: 因家廬山蓮花峰下。

translations.literal: He therefore made his home at the foot of Mount Lu's Lotus Peak.
translations.idiomatic: He made his home at the foot of Mount Lu's Lotus Peak.

sentences.zh: 前有溪，合于溢江，取營道所居濂溪以名之。

translations.literal: Before his dwelling was a stream that joined the Yi River; he took the name of the Lian Stream where he had lived in Yingdao and gave it to this place.
translations.idiomatic: A stream before his dwelling joined the Yi River; he named it Lian Stream after the stream of his native Yingdao.

sentences.zh: 抃再鎮蜀，將奏用之，未及而卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: When Bian was again stationed in Shu, he was about to memorialize recommending him for appointment, but before this could be done Dunyi died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Bian was again posted to Shu, he was preparing to recommend Dunyi for higher office, but Dunyi died before the memorial could be submitted. He was fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 黃庭堅稱其「人品甚高，胸懷灑落，如光風霽月。

translations.literal: Huang Tingjian praised him: "His personal character was very lofty, his breast open and unburdened, like a clear breeze after rain."
translations.idiomatic: Huang Tingjian praised him: "His character was of the highest order, his mind open and unburdened, like a clear breeze after rain has passed."

sentences.zh: 廉于取名而銳於求志，薄於徼福而厚於得民，菲於奉身而燕及煢嫠，陋於希世而尚友千古。」

translations.literal: Stingy in seeking fame yet keen in pursuing his aim, slight in praying for fortune yet generous in winning the people, frugal in providing for himself yet ample in reaching widows and orphans, disdainful of currying favor with the age yet honoring friendship with the ancients across a thousand ages."
translations.idiomatic: He was sparing in the pursuit of reputation but ardent in the pursuit of his ideals; indifferent to praying for personal fortune but generous in winning the people's hearts; austere in his own living but abundant in care for widows and orphans; contemptuous of worldly acclaim but devoted to friendship with the sages of antiquity."

sentences.zh: 博學行力，著《太極圖》，明天理之根源，究萬物之終始。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and forceful in practice, he authored the Diagram of the Supreme Pole, clarifying the root source of heavenly principle and investigating the beginning and end of the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned and rigorous in practice, he wrote the Diagram of the Supreme Pole, clarifying the root of heavenly principle and tracing the origin and end of all things.

sentences.zh: 其說曰：

translations.literal: His exposition says:
translations.idiomatic: His exposition reads:

sentences.zh: 無極而太極。

translations.literal: The limitless, and yet the Supreme Pole.
translations.idiomatic: The Limitless, and yet the Supreme Pole.

sentences.zh: 太極動而生陽，動極而靜，靜而生陰，靜極復動，一動一靜，互為其根，分陰分陽，兩儀立焉。

translations.literal: The Supreme Pole in movement generates yang; when movement reaches its extreme it becomes still, and in stillness yin is generated; when stillness reaches its extreme, movement returns again. One movement and one stillness are each the root of the other; yin and yang are differentiated, and the Two Modes are established.
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme Pole in movement generates yang; when movement reaches its limit it becomes still, and in stillness yin is generated; when stillness reaches its limit, movement arises again. Movement and stillness are each the root of the other; yin and yang are differentiated, and the Two Modes are established.

sentences.zh: 陽變陰合，而生水、火、木、金、土，五氣順布，四時行焉。

translations.literal: Yang transforms and yin combines, generating water, fire, wood, metal, and earth; the five qi are distributed in order, and the four seasons proceed thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Yang transforms and yin combines to generate water, fire, wood, metal, and earth; the five phases are distributed in proper order, and the four seasons proceed thereby.

sentences.zh: 五行一陰陽也，陰陽一太極也。

translations.literal: The five phases are one yin and yang; yin and yang are one Supreme Pole.
translations.idiomatic: The five phases are ultimately one yin and yang; yin and yang are ultimately one Supreme Pole.

sentences.zh: 太極本無極也。

translations.literal: The Supreme Pole is fundamentally the limitless.
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme Pole is fundamentally the Limitless.

sentences.zh: 五行之生也，各一其性。

translations.literal: In the generation of the five phases, each has its own nature.
translations.idiomatic: When the five phases arise, each possesses its own distinct nature.

sentences.zh: 無極之真，二五之精，妙合而凝，乾道成男，坤道成女。

translations.literal: The reality of the limitless, the essences of the two and five, wonderfully combine and coalesce; the Way of Qian forms the male, the Way of Kun forms the female.
translations.idiomatic: The reality of the Limitless and the essences of the two modes and five phases wonderfully combine and coalesce; the Way of Qian forms the male, the Way of Kun forms the female.

sentences.zh: 二氣交感，化生萬物，萬物生生，而變化無窮焉。

translations.literal: The two qi interact and generate the myriad things; the myriad things are born and reborn, and transformation is without end.
translations.idiomatic: The two qi interact and give birth to the myriad things; the myriad things are ceaselessly generated and transformed without end.

sentences.zh: 惟人也得其秀而最靈，形既生矣，神發知矣，五性感動而善惡分，萬事出矣。

translations.literal: Only humanity receives the finest essence and is most spiritually perceptive; once the form is generated, the spirit manifests awareness; the five natures are stirred and good and evil are divided, and the myriad affairs arise.
translations.idiomatic: Only humanity receives the finest essence of the two qi and is most spiritually perceptive. Once the physical form is generated, awareness arises; the five natures are stirred and good and evil are distinguished, and the myriad affairs of human life come forth.

sentences.zh: 聖人定之以中正仁義而主靜，立人極焉。

translations.literal: The sage fixes them with centrality, correctness, humaneness, and righteousness, taking stillness as primary, and establishes the human pole.
translations.idiomatic: The sage fixes them through centrality, correctness, humaneness, and righteousness, taking stillness as the foundation, and thereby establishes the human pole.

sentences.zh: 故聖人與天地合其德，日月合其明，四時合其序，鬼神合其吉凶。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage unites his virtue with Heaven and Earth, his brightness with sun and moon, his sequence with the four seasons, and his fortune and misfortune with spirits and ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the sage unites his virtue with Heaven and Earth, his clarity with the sun and moon, his order with the four seasons, and his judgment of fortune and misfortune with the spirits.

sentences.zh: 君子修之吉，小人悖之凶。

translations.literal: The gentleman who cultivates it finds good fortune; the petty man who violates it finds misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman who cultivates this path finds good fortune; the petty man who violates it meets with misfortune.

sentences.zh: 故曰：「立天之道，曰陰與陽。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: "To establish the Way of Heaven is called yin and yang."
translations.idiomatic: Hence it is said: "To establish the Way of Heaven is to name yin and yang."

sentences.zh: 立地之道，曰柔與剛。

translations.literal: To establish the Way of Earth is called yielding and firm.
translations.idiomatic: To establish the Way of Earth is to name yielding and firm.

sentences.zh: 立人之道，曰仁與義。

translations.literal: To establish the Way of Humanity is called humaneness and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: To establish the Way of Humanity is to name humaneness and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「原始反終，故知死生之說。

translations.literal: It is also said: "Tracing the origin and returning to the end, therefore one knows the explanation of life and death."
translations.idiomatic: It is also said: "By tracing things to their origin and returning to their end, one comprehends the meaning of life and death."

sentences.zh: 」大哉《易》也，斯其至矣。

translations.literal: How great is the Changes! This is its utmost reach.
translations.idiomatic: How great is the Book of Changes! In this lies its highest attainment.

sentences.zh: 又著《通書》四十篇，發明太極之蘊。

translations.literal: He also authored forty chapters of Penetrating the Book, elucidating the profundities of the Supreme Pole.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote forty chapters of Penetrating the Book, elucidating the full depth of the Supreme Pole.

sentences.zh: 序者謂「其言約而道大，文質而義精，得孔、孟之本源，大有功于學者也。」

translations.literal: The preface writer said: "Its words are concise yet the Way is great, its style plain yet its meaning refined; it attains the root source of Confucius and Mencius and has great merit for learners."
translations.idiomatic: The preface writer observed that "its language is concise yet the Way is vast, its style plain yet its meaning refined; it recovers the root source of Confucius and Mencius and renders great service to students of the Way."

sentences.zh: 掾南安時，程珦通判軍事，視其氣貌非常人，與語，知其為學知道，因與為友，使二子顥、頤往受業焉。

translations.literal: When he was an aide in Nan'an, Cheng Xiang was vice-prefect of the army; seeing Dunyi's bearing and appearance were not those of an ordinary man, and speaking with him, he knew him to be one who studied and knew the Way; he therefore befriended him and sent his two sons Hao and Yi to receive instruction from him.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in Nan'an, Dunyi met Cheng Xiang, who was vice-prefect of the prefecture. Seeing that Dunyi's bearing was unlike that of an ordinary man, and conversing with him, Cheng recognized a true scholar of the Way. He befriended Dunyi and sent his two sons, Hao and Yi, to study under him.

sentences.zh: 敦頤每令尋孔、顏樂處，所樂何事，二程之學源流乎此矣。

translations.literal: Dunyi often had them seek where Confucius and Yan Hui found their joy and what it was they delighted in; the source and flow of the two Chengs' learning originate here.
translations.idiomatic: Dunyi often directed them to discover what Confucius and Yan Hui found joyful and what it was they delighted in. The source of the two Chengs' learning lies here.

sentences.zh: 故顥之言曰：「自再見周茂叔後，吟風弄月以歸，有'吾與點也'之意。

translations.literal: Therefore Hao's words say: "After again seeing Zhou Maoshu, I returned home chanting of the wind and playing with the moon, with the meaning of 'I am with Dian.'"
translations.idiomatic: Hence Cheng Hao said: "After seeing Zhou Maoshu again, I returned home with the feeling of chanting in the breeze and enjoying the moonlight—as though I shared Zeng Dian's joy in the Spring and Autumn Annals."

sentences.zh: 」侯師聖學于程頤，未悟，訪敦頤，敦頤曰：「吾老矣，說不可不詳。

translations.literal: Hou Shisheng studied under Cheng Yi but had not yet awakened; he visited Dunyi. Dunyi said: "I am old—my explanation cannot but be thorough."
translations.idiomatic: Hou Shisheng studied under Cheng Yi but had not yet attained understanding. He visited Dunyi, who said, "I am old now—my explanation cannot be anything less than thorough."

sentences.zh: 」留對榻夜談，越三日乃還。

translations.literal: He kept him to converse face to face on a shared couch through the night; only after three days did he return.
translations.idiomatic: He kept Hou for three days and nights of conversation on a shared couch before allowing him to return.

sentences.zh: 頤驚異之，曰：「非從周茂叔來耶？

translations.literal: Yi was startled and wondered at this, saying: "Have you not come from Zhou Maoshu?"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi was astonished and said, "Surely you have just come from Zhou Maoshu?"

sentences.zh: 」其善開發人類此。

translations.literal: His skill in opening and developing people's understanding was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his gift for awakening understanding in others.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十三年，賜諡曰元公，淳祐元年，封汝南伯，從祀孔子廟庭。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiading, he was granted the posthumous title Lord Yuan; in the first year of Chunyou, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Runan and granted accompanying sacrifice in the court of Confucius's temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of the Jiading reign, he was granted the posthumous title Lord Yuan. In the first year of Chunyou, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Runan and granted accompanying sacrifice in the Confucian temple.

sentences.zh: 二子壽、燾，燾官至寶文閣待制。

translations.literal: His two sons were Shou and Tao; Tao reached the office of awaiting orders at the Hall of Treasured Literature.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Shou and Tao; Tao rose to the post of awaiting orders at the Hall of Treasured Literature.

sentences.zh: 程顥，字伯淳，世居中山，後從開封徙河南。

translations.literal: Cheng Hao, courtesy name Bochun, for generations dwelt in Zhongshan; later he followed the move from Kaifeng to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hao, styled Bochun, was descended from a family long settled in Zhongshan; later the family followed the court's move from Kaifeng to Henan.

sentences.zh: 高祖羽，太宗朝三司使。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yu was Commissioner of the Three Departments in the Taizong reign.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yu served as Commissioner of the Three Departments under Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 父珦，仁宗錄舊臣後，以為黃陂尉。

translations.literal: His father Xiang, when Emperor Renzong enrolled descendants of former ministers, was appointed magistrate of Huangpi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiang, enrolled among descendants of former ministers by Emperor Renzong, was appointed magistrate of Huangpi.

sentences.zh: 久之，知龔州。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was appointed prefect of Gongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was appointed prefect of Gongzhou.

sentences.zh: 時宜獠區希範既誅，鄉人忽傳其神降，言「當為我南海立祠」，於是迎其神以往，至龔，珦使詰之，曰：「比過潯，潯守以為妖，投祠具江中，逆流而上，守懼，乃更致禮。

translations.literal: At the time, after the Yao bandit Qu Xifan had been executed, the villagers suddenly spread word that his spirit had descended, saying "You must build a shrine for me in Nanhai"; they therefore welcomed his spirit and proceeded onward. When they reached Gong, Xiang sent someone to interrogate them. They said: "Just now passing Xun, the prefect of Xun regarded it as demonic, threw the shrine implements into the river, and they floated upstream against the current; the prefect was afraid and then offered proper rites again."
translations.idiomatic: After the Yao rebel Qu Xifan had been executed, villagers suddenly claimed that his spirit had descended, declaring that a shrine must be built for him in Nanhai. They carried his spirit image toward the south. When they reached Gongzhou, Xiang sent men to question them. They reported: "When we passed Xunzhou, the prefect there regarded it as demonic sorcery and threw the shrine implements into the river—but they floated upstream against the current. The prefect was terrified and offered proper rites instead."

sentences.zh: 」珦使復投之，順流去，其妄乃息。

translations.literal: Xiang had them throw the implements in again; they floated downstream and departed, and the delusion then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang had the implements thrown in again; this time they floated downstream and away, and the superstition subsided.

sentences.zh: 徙知磁州，又徙漢州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administer Cizhou, then again to Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Cizhou, and then to Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗宴客開元僧舍，酒方行，人歡言佛光見，觀者相騰踐，不可禁，珦安坐不動，頃之遂定。

translations.literal: Once while entertaining guests at the Kaiyuan monastery, as the wine was being served people cried out joyfully that a Buddhist light had appeared; the onlookers trampled and rushed upon one another and could not be restrained. Xiang sat unmoved, and in a moment all was calm.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while entertaining guests at the Kaiyuan Monastery, someone shouted that a Buddhist halo had appeared. The crowd stampeded in panic and could not be restrained. Xiang remained seated without moving, and in a moment calm was restored.

sentences.zh: 熙寧法行，為守令者奉命唯恐後，珦獨抗議，指其未便。

translations.literal: When the Xining laws were implemented, prefects and magistrates obeyed orders fearing to lag behind; Xiang alone protested, pointing out their inconveniences.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xining reforms were implemented, local officials rushed to comply for fear of falling behind. Xiang alone protested, pointing out their practical difficulties.

sentences.zh: 使者李元瑜怒，即移病歸，旋致仕，累轉太中大夫。

translations.literal: The commissioner Li Yuanyu was angry; Xiang immediately submitted notice of illness and returned home, soon retired from office, and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Li Yuanyu was enraged. Xiang promptly cited illness and returned home, soon retired from office, and was eventually promoted to Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 元祐五年，卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanyou he died, aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Yuanyou, at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 珦慈恕而剛斷，平居與幼賤處，唯恐有傷其意，至於犯義理，則不假也。

translations.literal: Xiang was compassionate and forgiving yet firm in judgment; in ordinary dealings with the young and lowly he always feared to wound their feelings, but when righteousness and principle were violated, he showed no indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was compassionate and forgiving yet firm in judgment. In daily dealings with the young and humble he was careful never to wound their feelings, but when principle was at stake he showed no indulgence.

sentences.zh: 左右使令之人，無日不察其饑飽寒燠。

translations.literal: For those attendants and servants at his side, not a day passed without his observing whether they were hungry or full, cold or warm.
translations.idiomatic: He never failed to notice whether the servants and attendants around him were hungry or full, cold or warm.

sentences.zh: 前後五得任子，以均諸父之子孫。

translations.literal: Five times he obtained the privilege of appointing a son to office, and used it to distribute equally among his father's brothers' descendants.
translations.idiomatic: On five occasions he received the privilege of appointing a son to office, and each time he distributed the benefit equally among his cousins.

sentences.zh: 嫁遣孤女，必盡其力。

translations.literal: In marrying off and providing dowries for orphaned girls, he always exerted his utmost effort.
translations.idiomatic: When marrying off orphaned girls, he always did everything in his power.

sentences.zh: 所得奉祿，分贍親戚之貧者。

translations.literal: The salary he received he divided to support poor relatives.
translations.idiomatic: He divided his salary to support impoverished relatives.

sentences.zh: 伯母寡居，奉養甚至。

translations.literal: His aunt by marriage lived as a widow; he supported her with the utmost care.
translations.idiomatic: He supported his widowed aunt with the utmost devotion.

sentences.zh: 從女兄既適人而喪其夫，珦迎以歸，教養其子，均于子侄。

translations.literal: His cousin by marriage, after marrying and losing her husband, was welcomed back by Xiang; he raised and educated her son, treating him equally with his own sons and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: When his cousin's husband died, Xiang welcomed her back into the household, raised and educated her son, and treated him no differently from his own sons and nephews.

sentences.zh: 時官小祿薄，克己為義，人以為難。

translations.literal: At that time officials held minor posts and thin salaries; to restrain oneself and act righteously was something people regarded as difficult.
translations.idiomatic: At a time when official posts were modest and salaries meager, to restrain oneself and live by principle was something people considered truly difficult.

sentences.zh: 文彥博、蘇頌等九人表其清節，詔賜帛二百，官給其葬。

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo, Su Song, and eight others jointly memorialized his pure integrity; an edict granted two hundred bolts of silk, and the government provided his burial.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo, Su Song, and seven others jointly memorialized his integrity; the throne responded with an edict granting two hundred bolts of silk and having the state provide his funeral.

sentences.zh: 顥舉進士，調鄮、上元主簿。

translations.literal: Hao passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk successively in Yin and Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hao passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk successively in Yin and Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 鄮民有借兄宅居者，發地得瘞錢，兄之子訴曰：「父所藏。

translations.literal: A Yin townsman who was borrowing his elder brother's house to live in dug up buried treasure money; the brother's son sued, saying: "My father buried it."
translations.idiomatic: In Yin County, a man who was renting his elder brother's house dug up buried treasure; the brother's son brought suit, claiming, "That was my father's hoard."

sentences.zh: 」顥問：「幾何年？

translations.literal: Hao asked: "How many years?"
translations.idiomatic: Hao asked, "How long ago was it buried?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「四十年。

translations.literal: He replied: "Forty years."
translations.idiomatic: The plaintiff answered, "Forty years ago."

sentences.zh: 」彼借居幾時？

translations.literal: How long has he been borrowing the house to live in?
translations.idiomatic: How long has the tenant been living in the house?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「二十年矣。

translations.literal: He replied: "Twenty years now."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Twenty years."

sentences.zh: 」遣吏取十千視之，謂訴者曰：「今官所鑄錢，不五六年即遍天下，此皆未藏前數十年所鑄，何也？

translations.literal: Hao sent an official to fetch ten thousand coins to examine them, and said to the plaintiff: "The coins currently minted by the government, within five or six years spread throughout the realm; these were all minted decades before the burial—why is that?"
translations.idiomatic: Hao sent a clerk to fetch ten thousand coins for inspection and said to the plaintiff, "Coins minted by the government today circulate throughout the realm within five or six years. These were all cast decades before the burial—how do you explain that?"

sentences.zh: 」其人不能答。

translations.literal: That man could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The man had no reply.

sentences.zh: 茅山有池，產龍如蜥蜴而五色。

translations.literal: On Mount Mao there was a pool that produced dragons like lizards but in five colors.
translations.idiomatic: On Mount Mao there was a pool whose "dragons" were lizard-like creatures in five colors.

sentences.zh: 祥符中嘗取二龍入都，半塗失其一，中使雲飛空而逝。

translations.literal: In the Xiangfu era two dragons were once taken to the capital; halfway there one was lost—a palace envoy said it flew into the sky and departed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiangfu reign, two of these creatures were once sent to the capital; halfway there one vanished, and a palace envoy claimed it had flown into the sky and escaped.

sentences.zh: 民俗嚴奉不懈，顥捕而脯之。

translations.literal: Local custom strictly venerated them without slackening; Hao captured them and had them cured as dried meat.
translations.idiomatic: The local people revered them with unwavering devotion; Hao had them captured and cured into jerky.

sentences.zh: 為晉城令，富人張氏父死，旦有老叟踵門曰：「我，汝父也。

translations.literal: Serving as magistrate of Jincheng, when a rich man's Zhang's father died, at dawn an old man came to the door saying: "I am your father."
translations.idiomatic: While serving as magistrate of Jincheng, Hao encountered a case in which a wealthy Zhang's father had died; at dawn an old man came to the door and declared, "I am your father."

sentences.zh: 」子驚疑莫測，相與詣縣。

translations.literal: The son, shocked and uncertain, went together with him to the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: The son, astonished and unable to fathom the claim, went with him to the magistrate's office.

sentences.zh: 叟曰：「身為醫，遠出治疾，而妻生子，貧不能養，以與張。

translations.literal: The old man said: "I was a physician, went far away to treat illness, and my wife gave birth to a son; being poor and unable to raise him, I gave him to the Zhang family."
translations.idiomatic: The old man said, "I was a physician. I went far away to treat the sick, and while I was gone my wife bore a son. Too poor to raise him, I gave the child to the Zhang family."

sentences.zh: 」顥質其驗。

translations.literal: Hao tested the evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Hao examined the evidence.

sentences.zh: 取懷中一書進，其所記曰：「某年月日，抱兒與張三翁家。

translations.literal: The old man took from his bosom a book and presented it; what was recorded said: "On such-and-such year, month, and day, I carried the infant to the house of Old Zhang Three."
translations.idiomatic: The old man produced a book from his robe; it recorded, "On such-and-such a date I carried the infant to the home of Old Zhang Three."

sentences.zh: 」顥問：「張是時才四十，安得有翁稱？

translations.literal: Hao asked: "Zhang was then only forty—how could he have been called 'Old'?"
translations.idiomatic: Hao asked, "Zhang was only forty at the time—how could he have been called 'Old Zhang'?"

sentences.zh: 」叟駭謝。

translations.literal: The old man, alarmed, apologized.
translations.idiomatic: The old man, startled, confessed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 民稅粟多移近邊，載往則道遠，就糴則價高。

translations.literal: The people's grain tax often had to be transported to near the border; carrying it there meant long roads, while buying grain locally meant high prices.
translations.idiomatic: The people's grain tax often had to be delivered to frontier depots; transporting it meant long hauls, while purchasing grain locally meant steep prices.

sentences.zh: 顥擇富而可任者，預使貯粟以待，費大省。

translations.literal: Hao selected wealthy men who could be entrusted, and beforehand had them store grain to await collection; expenses were greatly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Hao selected wealthy men of proven reliability and had them store grain in advance against the tax levy, greatly reducing the cost.

sentences.zh: 民以事至縣者，必告以孝弟忠信，入所以事其父兄，出所以事其長上。

translations.literal: Whenever people came to the county on business, he always instructed them in filial piety, brotherly respect, loyalty, and trustworthiness—what to use at home in serving fathers and elder brothers, and what to use outside in serving superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever people came to the county on business, he always instructed them in filial piety, brotherly respect, loyalty, and trustworthiness—how to conduct themselves at home toward fathers and elder brothers, and how to conduct themselves abroad toward superiors.

sentences.zh: 度鄉村遠近為伍保，使之力役相助，患難相恤，而奸偽無所容。

translations.literal: He measured the distance of villages and grouped them into five- and ten-household units, enabling them to help one another in corvée and mutual aid in hardship, so that trickery and fraud had nowhere to hide.
translations.idiomatic: He measured the distances between villages and organized them into mutual-responsibility groups of five and ten households, so that they could assist one another in labor and in hardship, leaving no room for fraud.

sentences.zh: 凡孤煢殘廢者，責之親戚鄉党，使無失所。

translations.literal: For all who were orphaned, bereft, crippled, or disabled, he charged kin and neighbors to ensure none were left without support.
translations.idiomatic: For all who were orphaned, widowed, crippled, or disabled, he held relatives and neighbors responsible so that none were left destitute.

sentences.zh: 行旅出於其途者，疾病皆有所養。

translations.literal: Travelers passing through his jurisdiction who fell ill all had places of care.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers who fell ill along the roads within his jurisdiction were all given care.

sentences.zh: 鄉必有校，暇時親至，召父老與之語。

translations.literal: Every township had a school; in his free time he personally visited, summoning elders to converse with them.
translations.idiomatic: Every township had a school; in his spare time he visited in person, summoning the village elders to speak with them.

sentences.zh: 兒童所讀書，親為正句讀，教者不善，則為易置。

translations.literal: For books the children were reading, he personally corrected punctuation and phrasing; if a teacher was inadequate, he replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: He personally corrected the texts the children were reading and marked the phrasing; if a teacher proved incompetent, he replaced him.

sentences.zh: 擇子弟之秀者，聚而教之。

translations.literal: He selected outstanding sons and nephews of the district and gathered them to teach.
translations.idiomatic: He selected the most promising young men of the district and gathered them for instruction.

sentences.zh: 鄉民為社會，為立科條，旌別善惡，使有勸有恥。

translations.literal: When villagers formed communal associations, he established regulations for them, distinguishing good from evil so there would be both encouragement and shame.
translations.idiomatic: When villagers formed communal associations, he drew up rules for them, distinguishing good from evil so that virtue would be rewarded and vice shamed.

sentences.zh: 在縣三歲，民愛之如父母。

translations.literal: After three years in the county, the people loved him as they would their own parents.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office, the people loved him as they would their own parents.

sentences.zh: 熙甯初，用呂公著薦，為太子中允、監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xining era, on Lü Gongzhu's recommendation, he became Senior Recorder in the Heir Apparent's Palace and acting Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of the Xining reforms, on the recommendation of Lü Gongzhu, he was appointed Senior Recorder in the Heir Apparent's Palace and acting Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 神宗素知其名，數召見，每退，必曰：「頻求對，欲常常見卿。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong had long known his reputation and summoned him many times; each time he withdrew, the emperor always said: "Petition frequently for audience—I wish to see you often."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong had long known his name and summoned him repeatedly; each time Hao withdrew, the Emperor would say, "Petition often for an audience—I want to see you frequently."

sentences.zh: 」一日，從容咨訪，報正午，始趨出，庭中人曰：「御史不知上未食乎？

translations.literal: One day, in relaxed consultation, the report came that it was midday before he hurried out; someone in the courtyard said: "Does the censor not know the Emperor has not yet eaten?"
translations.idiomatic: One day, during an unhurried consultation, the noon drum sounded before Hao finally hurried out; someone in the courtyard remarked, "Does the censor not know the Emperor has not yet eaten?"

sentences.zh: 」前後進說甚多，大要以正心窒欲、求賢育材為言，務以誠意感悟主上。

translations.literal: Before and after he made many presentations, largely speaking of rectifying the mind, restraining desires, seeking worthies, and nurturing talent, striving to move the sovereign with sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Over time he made many presentations, chiefly urging the rectification of the mind, the restraint of desire, the seeking of worthy men, and the nurturing of talent, striving always to move the sovereign through sincerity.

sentences.zh: 嘗勸帝防未萌之欲，及勿輕天下士，帝俯躬曰：「當為卿戒之。」

translations.literal: He once urged the Emperor to guard against desires before they sprouted, and not to slight men of talent throughout the realm; the Emperor bowed and said: "I shall take this as a warning on your account."
translations.idiomatic: He once urged the Emperor to guard against desires before they took root and not to slight the talented men of the realm; the Emperor bowed and said, "I shall heed your warning."

sentences.zh: 王安石執政，議更法令，中外皆不以為便，言者攻之甚力。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi took power and proposed changing laws and regulations; inside and outside the court all regarded it as inconvenient, and critics attacked it vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi came to power and proposed revising the laws, people throughout the court and the country alike found the changes burdensome, and critics attacked them fiercely.

sentences.zh: 顥被旨赴中堂議事，安石方怒言者，厲色待之。

translations.literal: Hao received an order to go to the Central Hall to discuss affairs; Anshi was then angry at the critics and awaited him with a fierce expression.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was ordered to the Central Hall to discuss policy; Wang Anshi, still furious at his critics, received him with a stern face.

sentences.zh: 顥徐曰：「天下事非一家私議，願平氣以聽。

translations.literal: Hao calmly said: "Affairs of the realm are not one family's private deliberation—I hope you will listen with equanimity."
translations.idiomatic: Hao said calmly, "The affairs of the realm are not a private matter for one family to decide—I ask that you listen with an even temper."

sentences.zh: 」安石為之愧屈。

translations.literal: Anshi was shamed and subdued by this.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi was shamed into silence.

sentences.zh: 自安石用事，顥未嘗一語及于功利。

translations.literal: Since Anshi wielded power, Hao never once spoke of profit and utility.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Anshi took charge of affairs, Hao never once addressed questions of profit and expedience.

sentences.zh: 居職八九月，數論時政，最後言曰：「智者若禹之行水，行其所無事也；

translations.literal: After eight or nine months in office, he repeatedly discoursed on current policies; finally he said: "The wise are like Yu in channeling water—they go where there is no obstruction;"
translations.idiomatic: After eight or nine months in office, he repeatedly addressed current policy; in his final memorial he said, "The wise ruler is like Yu guiding water—he follows the path of least resistance;"

sentences.zh: 舍而之險阻，不足以言智。

translations.literal: to abandon that and go toward peril and obstruction—is not enough to be called wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: to abandon that and force a course through danger and obstruction is not wisdom at all.

sentences.zh: 自古興治立事，未有中外人情交謂不可而能有成者，況于排斥忠良，沮廢公議，用賤陵貴，以邪幹正者乎？

translations.literal: Since antiquity in establishing good governance and undertaking affairs, there has never been one who succeeded when court and realm alike jointly regarded it impossible—how much less when driving out the loyal and good, obstructing and discarding public discussion, using the base to override the noble, and employing the wrong to interfere with the right?
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, no undertaking of governance has ever succeeded when everyone inside and outside the court agreed it could not—much less when the loyal are driven out, public debate suppressed, the lowly allowed to override the worthy, and wrong used to obstruct right.

sentences.zh: 正使徼幸有小成，而興利之臣日進，尚德之風浸衰，尤非朝廷之福。

translations.literal: Even if by chance there were minor success, yet men seeking profit would daily advance while the ethos of revering virtue would gradually decay—this is especially no blessing to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Even if one were to scrape together a few small gains, the men of profit would advance day by day while the spirit of reverence for virtue would steadily fade—far from a blessing to the court.

sentences.zh: 」遂乞去言職。

translations.literal: He thereupon requested to leave his remonstrance post.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon requested to be relieved of his remonstrance duties.

sentences.zh: 安石本與之善，及是雖不合，猶敬其忠信，不深怒，但出提點京西刑獄。

translations.literal: Anshi had originally been on good terms with him; though they no longer agreed, he still respected his loyalty and trustworthiness and did not deeply rage, merely posting him out as Judicial Intendant of the Western Capital Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi had originally been on good terms with him; though they now disagreed, he still respected Hao's loyalty and integrity and did not punish him severely, merely transferring him to serve as Judicial Intendant of the Western Capital Circuit.

sentences.zh: 顥固辭，改簽書鎮甯軍判官。

translations.literal: Hao firmly declined and was instead reassigned as signing secretary and military judge of Zhenning Army.
translations.idiomatic: Hao firmly declined the post and was instead reassigned as signing secretary and administrative aide of Zhenning Army.

sentences.zh: 司馬光在長安，上疏求退，稱顥公直，以為己所不如。

translations.literal: Sima Guang, in Chang'an, memorialized requesting retirement, praising Hao's uprightness and deeming himself Hao's inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang, then in Chang'an, memorialized requesting retirement and praised Hao's uprightness, declaring himself Hao's inferior.

sentences.zh: 程昉治河，取澶卒八百而虐用之，眾逃歸。

translations.literal: Cheng Fang was managing the river works, took eight hundred soldiers from Dizhou and abused them; the masses fled and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Fang, who was overseeing river works, requisitioned eight hundred soldiers from Dizhou and worked them brutally; the men deserted and fled home.

sentences.zh: 群僚畏昉，欲勿納。

translations.literal: The group of officials feared Fang and wished not to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: The officials, fearing Cheng Fang, wanted to refuse them entry.

sentences.zh: 顥曰：「彼逃死自歸，弗納必亂。

translations.literal: Hao said: "They fled death and returned of themselves—if not received, disorder is inevitable."
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "They fled for their lives and returned on their own—if we refuse them, there will surely be unrest."

sentences.zh: 若昉怒，吾自任之。

translations.literal: If Fang is angry, I myself will take responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: If Cheng Fang is angry, I will take full responsibility myself."

sentences.zh: 」即親往啟門拊勞，約少休三日復役，眾歡踴而入。

translations.literal: He immediately went in person, opened the gates, patted and comforted them, agreed they would rest three days and then return to service; the crowd joyfully leaped forward and entered.
translations.idiomatic: He went in person, opened the gates, and comforted the men, agreeing that they might rest three days before returning to labor; the soldiers entered cheering.

sentences.zh: 具以事上，得不遣。

translations.literal: He fully reported the matter upward and was able to avoid having them sent back.
translations.idiomatic: He reported the full circumstances to the court and secured permission to keep the men.

sentences.zh: 昉後過州，揚言曰：「澶卒之潰，蓋程中允誘之，吾且訴於上。

translations.literal: Later Fang passed through the prefecture and declared publicly: "The collapse of the Dizhou soldiers was surely induced by Junior Supervisor Cheng—I shall appeal to the throne."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Cheng Fang passed through the prefecture, he declared publicly, "The desertion of the Dizhou soldiers was instigated by Junior Supervisor Cheng—I intend to lodge a complaint with the throne."

sentences.zh: 」顥聞之，曰：「彼方憚我，何能為。

translations.literal: Hearing this, Hao said: "He is just then in awe of me—what can he do?"
translations.idiomatic: When Hao heard this, he said, "He is still afraid of me—what can he do?"

sentences.zh: 」果不敢言。

translations.literal: In the end he did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Cheng Fang did not dare carry out his threat.

sentences.zh: 曹村埽決，顥謂郡守劉渙曰：「曹村決，京師可虞。

translations.literal: The Cao Village embankment breached; Hao said to Prefect Liu Huan: "If Cao Village breaks, the capital will be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: When the Cao Village levee burst, Hao said to Prefect Liu Huan, "If Cao Village is not sealed, the capital itself will be at risk."

sentences.zh: 臣子之分，身可塞亦所當為，盍盡遣廂卒見付。

translations.literal: The duty of subject and minister—if one's body can block the breach, that too is what ought to be done—why not send all your garrison soldiers to me?"
translations.idiomatic: It is the duty of a subject to give his body if it can block the breach—send me all the garrison troops you have."

sentences.zh: 」渙以鎮印付顥，立走決所，激諭士卒。

translations.literal: Huan handed the military seal to Hao, who immediately ran to the breach site and roused and admonished the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huan entrusted him with the military seal; Hao ran straight to the breach and rallied the troops.

sentences.zh: 議者以為勢不可塞，徒勞人爾。

translations.literal: Discussants thought the situation could not be blocked—it would only waste men.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers judged the breach beyond repair and the effort a waste of manpower.

sentences.zh: 顥命善泅者度決口，引巨索濟眾，兩岸並進，數日而合。

translations.literal: Hao ordered skilled swimmers to cross the breach, guided great ropes to ferry the mass, advanced on both banks simultaneously, and in several days closed it.
translations.idiomatic: Hao sent skilled swimmers across the breach to carry great ropes, ferried men and materials across, and advanced from both banks until the gap was closed within days.

sentences.zh: 求監洛河竹木務，歷年不敘伐閱，特遷太常丞。

translations.literal: He requested to supervise the Lu River Bamboo and Timber Office; years passed without promotion review, but he was specially promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He requested appointment to supervise the Lu River Bamboo and Timber Office; though years passed without a routine merit review, he was specially promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 帝又欲使修《三經義》，執政不可，命知扶溝縣。

translations.literal: The Emperor also wished to have him compile the Exegesis of the Three Classics; the chief ministers objected and he was ordered to serve as magistrate of Fugou County.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also wished to have him compile the Exegesis of the Three Classics, but the chief ministers objected, and he was instead appointed magistrate of Fugou County.

sentences.zh: 廣濟、蔡河在縣境，瀕河惡子無生理，專脅取行舟財貨，歲必焚舟十數以立威。

translations.literal: The Guangji and Cai canals were within the county borders; ruffians along the river had no livelihood and specialized in extorting goods from passing boats, every year burning a dozen or so boats to establish dread.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangji and Cai canals ran through the county; riverfront ruffians with no honest livelihood made a living extorting passing boats and burned a dozen or more vessels each year to intimidate travelers.

sentences.zh: 顥捕得一人，使引其類，貰宿惡，分地處之，令以挽繂為業，且察為奸者，自是境無焚剽患。

translations.literal: Hao captured one man, had him lead out his kind, pardoned their old crimes, assigned them land to settle on, ordered them to take towing as their occupation, and watched for those who committed evil—from then on within the jurisdiction there was no scourge of burning and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Hao arrested one ringleader and had him identify his accomplices; he pardoned their past crimes, settled them on allotted land, and put them to work as boat haulers, keeping watch for any who returned to crime—after which the county was free of arson and robbery along the waterways.

sentences.zh: 內侍王中正按閱保甲，權焰章震，諸邑競侈供張悅之，主吏來請，顥曰：「吾邑貧，安能效他邑。

translations.literal: Palace Intendant Wang Zhongzheng inspected the militia; his authority blazed conspicuously; all counties vied in extravagant provisions to please him; the chief clerk came to request funds; Hao said: "Our county is poor—how can we imitate other counties?"
translations.idiomatic: When the palace intendant Wang Zhongzheng came to inspect the militia, his power was on full display; every county competed to lavish entertainment upon him. When the chief clerk came to request funds, Hao said, "Our county is poor—how can we match the extravagance of other counties?"

sentences.zh: 取於民，法所禁也，獨有令故青帳可用爾。

translations.literal: To take from the people is forbidden by law; only the old blue tent from previous magistrates may be used."
translations.idiomatic: To levy supplies from the people is forbidden by law. All we can offer is the old blue tent left by a former magistrate."

sentences.zh: 」除判武學，李定劾其新法之初首為異論，罷歸故官。

translations.literal: He was appointed judge of the Military Academy; Li Ding impeached him for at the outset of the new laws being the first to offer dissenting views, and he was dismissed and returned to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed administrative judge of the Military Academy, but Li Ding impeached him for having been among the first to oppose the new laws at their inception, and he was dismissed and returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 又坐獄逸囚，責監汝州鹽稅。

translations.literal: He was again punished because a prisoner escaped from jail and was assigned to supervise the salt tax of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished again when a prisoner escaped from custody and was demoted to supervisor of the salt tax in Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，召為宗正丞，未行而卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended, he was summoned as Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court but died before taking up the post, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, Hao was summoned to serve as Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, but died before taking up the appointment, at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 顥資性過人，充養有道，和粹之氣，盎於面背，門人交友從之數十年，亦未嘗見其忿厲之容。

translations.literal: Hao's natural endowment surpassed others; his self-cultivation followed the Way; a harmonious purity filled his face and back; disciples and friends who followed him for decades also never saw an angry or harsh countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's native gifts surpassed those of ordinary men, and his moral cultivation was thorough; an air of harmonious clarity radiated from him; disciples and friends who kept company with him for decades never once saw anger or severity on his face.

sentences.zh: 遇事優為，雖當倉卒，不動聲色。

translations.literal: In handling affairs he was at ease; even in sudden emergencies, his voice and color did not change.
translations.idiomatic: He handled affairs with unhurried composure; even in sudden crises, his voice and expression never changed.

sentences.zh: 自十五六時，與弟頤聞汝南周敦頤論學，遂厭科舉之習，慨然有求道之志。

translations.literal: From age fifteen or sixteen, he and his younger brother Yi heard Zhou Dunyi of Runan discourse on learning, then came to loathe the habits of the examination system and grandly conceived the resolve to seek the Way.
translations.idiomatic: From the age of fifteen or sixteen, he and his younger brother Yi heard Zhou Dunyi of Runan expound the learning of the sages; they came to despise the habits of the examination system and resolved with passion to seek the Way.

sentences.zh: 氾濫于諸家，出入於老、釋者幾十年，返求諸《六經》而後得之。

translations.literal: He wandered broadly among various schools, going in and out of Laozi and Buddhism for nearly ten years, then turned to seek in the Six Classics before attaining it.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged widely through the teachings of many schools, passing in and out of Daoist and Buddhist learning for nearly ten years, before turning back to the Six Classics and finding what he sought.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢以來，未有臻斯理者。

translations.literal: Since Qin and Han, there had been none who reached this principle.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Qin and Han dynasties, no one had attained this understanding.

sentences.zh: 教人自致知至於知止，誠意至於平天下，灑掃應對至於窮理盡性，循循有序。

translations.literal: In teaching people, from extending knowledge to reaching cessation, from making intentions sincere to pacifying the realm, from sweeping and responding to fathoming principle and exhausting nature—step by step in ordered sequence.
translations.idiomatic: In teaching others, he moved step by step in proper order—from extending knowledge to reaching stillness, from making the will sincere to bringing peace to the realm, from sweeping the floor and answering questions to fathoming principle and exhausting nature.

sentences.zh: 病學者厭卑近而鶩高遠，卒無成焉，故其言曰：「道之不明，異端害之也。

translations.literal: He lamented that learners despise the humble and near while rushing toward the lofty and far, and ultimately achieve nothing; hence his words: "That the Way is unclear—heterodox teachings harm it."
translations.idiomatic: He deplored the tendency of students to scorn what is humble and near at hand while chasing what is lofty and remote, and so achieve nothing; hence his saying, "The Way has grown obscure because heterodox teachings have harmed it."

sentences.zh: 昔之害近而易知，今之害深而難辨。

translations.literal: Past harms were near and easy to know; present harms are deep and hard to distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: The harm of old was near at hand and easy to recognize; the harm of today runs deep and is hard to discern.

sentences.zh: 昔之惑人也乘其迷暗，今之惑人也因其高明。

translations.literal: Past deceivers of people exploited their confusion and darkness; present deceivers exploit their loftiness and brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, false teachings preyed on people's ignorance and confusion; today they prey on their intelligence and refinement.

sentences.zh: 自謂之窮神知化，而不足以開物成務，言為無不周遍，實則外於倫理，窮深極微，而不可以入堯、舜之道。

translations.literal: Calling themselves those who exhaust spirit and know transformation, yet insufficient to open things and accomplish affairs; in speech nothing not comprehensive, yet in reality outside human relations; probing depth and reaching the subtle, yet unable to enter the Way of Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: They call themselves masters of probing spirit and comprehending transformation, yet cannot open the way to practical achievement; their words seem all-encompassing, yet in truth they stand outside human relations; they probe the deepest and subtlest mysteries, yet cannot enter the Way of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 天下之學，非淺陋固滯，則必入於此。

translations.literal: Learning throughout the realm, if not shallow, crude, and rigidly stuck, then necessarily enters into this.
translations.idiomatic: Learning throughout the realm, if it is not shallow, crude, and hidebound, inevitably falls into this error.

sentences.zh: 自道之不明也，邪誕妖妄之說競起，塗生民之耳目，溺天下於污濁，雖高才明智，膠於見聞，醉生夢死，不自覺也。

translations.literal: Since the Way has been unclear, perverse, absurd, and fantastical doctrines have competed to rise, smearing the ears and eyes of the people, drowning the realm in filth; even those of high talent and clear wisdom, glued to what they have seen and heard, live drunk and die dreaming without self-awareness.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Way fell into obscurity, perverse and fantastic doctrines have sprung up in rivalry, befouling the ears and eyes of the people and drowning the world in corruption; even men of high talent and keen intelligence, trapped by what they have seen and heard, live as if drunk and die as if dreaming, never waking to the truth.

sentences.zh: 是皆正路之蓁蕪，聖門之蔽塞，辟之而後可以入道。」

translations.literal: All these are weeds on the right path, blockages at the sage's gate—only after clearing them can one enter the Way."
translations.idiomatic: All of these are weeds choking the true path and obstructions blocking the sage's gate; only after clearing them away can one enter the Way."

sentences.zh: 顥之死，士大夫識與不識，莫不哀傷焉。

translations.literal: At Hao's death, scholar-officials whether acquainted or not, none did not grieve.
translations.idiomatic: At Hao's death, scholar-officials throughout the realm, whether they had known him or not, grieved.

sentences.zh: 文彥博采眾論，題其墓曰明道先生。

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo gathered public opinion and inscribed his tomb "Master Mingdao."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo collected the consensus of opinion and inscribed his tomb with the title Master Mingdao.

sentences.zh: 其弟頤序之曰：「周公沒，聖人之道不行；

translations.literal: His younger brother Yi wrote in the preface: "When the Duke of Zhou died, the Way of the sage did not go forth;"
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yi wrote in the preface, "When the Duke of Zhou died, the Way of the sage ceased to be practiced;"

sentences.zh: 孟軻死，聖人之學不傳。

translations.literal: when Mencius died, the learning of the sage was not transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: when Mencius died, the learning of the sage ceased to be transmitted.

sentences.zh: 道不行，百世無善治；

translations.literal: When the Way does not go forth, for a hundred generations there is no good governance;
translations.idiomatic: When the Way is not practiced, good government fails for a hundred generations;

sentences.zh: 學不傳，千載無真儒。

translations.literal: when learning is not transmitted, for a thousand years there are no true Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: when learning is not transmitted, no true Confucian appears for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 無善治，士猶得以明夫善治之道，以淑諸人，以傳諸後；

translations.literal: Without good governance, gentlemen can still clarify the Way of good governance, to beautify people with it and transmit it to posterity;
translations.idiomatic: Without good government, gentlemen may still clarify the principles of good government, refine others through them, and pass them on to posterity;

sentences.zh: 無真儒，則貿貿焉莫知所之，人欲肆而天理滅矣。

translations.literal: without true Confucians, then blindly one knows not whither to go, human desires run riot and Heavenly principle is extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: but without true Confucians, people wander blindly with no direction, human desire runs unchecked, and Heavenly principle is extinguished.

sentences.zh: 先生生於千四百年之後，得不傳之學於遺經，以興起斯文為己任，辨異喘，辟邪說，使聖人之道煥然復明于世，蓋自孟子之後，一人而已。

translations.literal: The Master was born more than fourteen hundred years later, obtained the untransmitted learning from surviving classics, took reviving this culture as his own charge, distinguished heterodox doctrines, repelled evil doctrines, and made the Way of the sage blaze anew in the world—since Mencius, only this one man.
translations.idiomatic: Born more than fourteen hundred years later, the Master recovered the untransmitted learning from the surviving classics, took upon himself the task of reviving this culture, distinguished heterodox doctrines, and repelled perverse teachings, causing the Way of the sage to shine forth anew in the world—in the entire span since Mencius, he alone.

sentences.zh: 然學者于道不知所向，則孰知斯人之為功；

translations.literal: Yet if learners of the Way know not where it leads, then who knows this man's achievement;
translations.idiomatic: Yet if students of the Way do not know where it leads, who can grasp this man's achievement;

sentences.zh: 不知所至，則孰知斯名之稱情也哉。」

translations.literal: if they know not where it arrives, then who knows that this name fits the truth!"
translations.idiomatic: if they do not know where it ends, who can understand that this title is truly deserved?"

sentences.zh: 嘉定十三年，賜諡曰純公。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiading, he was posthumously granted the temple name Duke Chun.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of the Jiading reign, he was posthumously granted the title Duke Chun.

sentences.zh: 淳祐元年封河南伯，從祀孔子廟庭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunyou he was enfeoffed as Baron of Henan and granted attendant sacrifice in Confucius's temple courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Chunyou reign he was enfeoffed as Baron of Henan and granted a place in attendant sacrifice at the Confucian temple.

sentences.zh: 程頤，字正叔。

translations.literal: Cheng Yi, courtesy name Zhengshu.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi, styled Zhengshu.

sentences.zh: 年十八，上書闕下，欲天子黜世俗之論，以王道為心。

translations.literal: At age eighteen, he submitted a memorial at the palace gates, wishing the Son of Heaven to dismiss vulgar doctrines and take the kingly Way as his heart.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he submitted a memorial at the palace gates, urging the Son of Heaven to set aside vulgar doctrines and take the kingly Way to heart.

sentences.zh: 游太學，見胡瑗問諸生以顏子所好何學，頤因答曰：

translations.literal: While studying at the Imperial Academy, he saw Hu Yuan ask the students what learning Yanzi favored, and Yi thereupon answered:
translations.idiomatic: While at the Imperial Academy, he saw Hu Yuan ask the students what learning Yan Hui cherished, and Cheng Yi thereupon replied:

sentences.zh: 學以至聖人之道也。

translations.literal: Learning is to reach the Way of the sage.
translations.idiomatic: "Learning is the means of reaching the sage's Way."

sentences.zh: 聖人可學而至歟？

translations.literal: Can the sage be reached through learning?
translations.idiomatic: "Can one attain sagehood through learning?"

sentences.zh: 曰：然。

translations.literal: He said: Yes.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Yes."

sentences.zh: 學之道如何？

translations.literal: What is the Way of learning?
translations.idiomatic: "What is the Way of learning?"

sentences.zh: 曰：天地儲精，得五行之秀者為人，其本也真而靜，其未發也。

translations.literal: He said: Heaven and earth store essence; those who receive the finest of the Five Phases become human—whose root is genuine and still, before it is stirred.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Heaven and earth store their essence, and those who receive the finest of the Five Phases become human beings. Their root is genuine and still, before it has stirred."

sentences.zh: 五性具焉，曰仁、義、禮、智、信。

translations.literal: The five natures are complete therein, namely benevolence, righteousness, ritual, wisdom, and trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: "The five natures are complete in them: benevolence, righteousness, ritual, wisdom, and trustworthiness."

sentences.zh: 形既生矣，外物觸其形而動其中矣，其中動而七情出焉，曰喜、怒、哀、樂、愛、惡、欲。

translations.literal: Once the form is born, external things touch the form and move what is within; when what is within moves, the seven emotions emerge, namely joy, anger, sorrow, delight, love, hatred, and desire.
translations.idiomatic: "Once the body is formed, external things touch it and stir what lies within; when the inner self is stirred, the seven emotions emerge—joy, anger, sorrow, pleasure, love, hatred, and desire."

sentences.zh: 情既熾而益蕩，其性鑿矣。

translations.literal: When emotions grow intense and increasingly restless, one's nature is chipped away.
translations.idiomatic: "When emotions flare and grow ever more unruly, the nature is worn away."

sentences.zh: 是故覺者約其情使合於中，正其心，養其性；

translations.literal: Therefore the awakened person restrains emotions so they accord with the center, rectifies the heart, and nurtures one's nature;
translations.idiomatic: "Therefore the awakened person restrains the emotions to keep them in accord with the Mean, rectifies the heart, and nurtures the nature;"

sentences.zh: 愚者則不知制之，縱其情而至於邪僻，梏其性而亡之。

translations.literal: The fool does not know to control them, indulges emotions until they turn depraved, shackles one's nature, and destroys it.
translations.idiomatic: "while the fool does not know how to restrain them, indulges his emotions until they turn depraved, and by shackling his nature destroys it."

sentences.zh: 然學之道，必先明諸心，知所養；

translations.literal: Now the Way of learning must first clarify the heart, knowing what to nurture;
translations.idiomatic: "Yet the Way of learning must first clarify the heart and know what to nurture;"

sentences.zh: 然後力行以求至，所謂「自明而誠」也。

translations.literal: Then earnestly practice to reach it—what is called "from clarity to sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: "then earnestly put it into practice to reach the goal—what is called 'from clarity to sincerity.'"

sentences.zh: 誠之之道，在乎通道篤，通道篤則行之果，行之果則守之固，仁義忠信不離乎心，造次必於是，顛沛必於是，出處語默必於是，久而弗失，則居之安，動容周旋中禮，而邪僻之心無自生矣。

translations.literal: The Way of sincerity lies in profound penetration of the Way—when the Way is profoundly penetrated, practice is resolute; when practice is resolute, steadfastness is firm; benevolence, righteousness, loyalty, and trustworthiness do not leave the heart; in haste one acts thus, in distress one acts thus, in going out and staying in, in speech and silence one acts thus; long without losing it, then one dwells securely, and in every movement and gesture one's conduct accords with ritual, and no depraved heart arises of itself.
translations.idiomatic: "The Way of sincerity lies in profound penetration of the Way. When the Way is profoundly penetrated, practice is resolute; when practice is resolute, steadfastness is secure. Benevolence, righteousness, loyalty, and trustworthiness never leave the heart—in haste one holds to them, in distress one holds to them, whether going out or staying in, speaking or silent. Maintained long without loss, one dwells at ease; every movement and gesture accords with ritual, and no depraved inclination arises on its own."

sentences.zh: 故顏子所事，則曰：「非禮勿視，非禮勿聽，非禮勿言，非禮勿動。
