translations.literal: Therefore what Yanzi practiced, he said: "Do not look at what is not ritual; do not listen to what is not ritual; do not speak what is not ritual; do not act in what is not ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Thus what Yanzi put into practice, he said: "Look not at what violates ritual; listen not to what violates ritual; speak not what violates ritual; move not in what violates ritual."

sentences.zh: 」仲尼稱之，則曰：「得一善則拳拳服膺而弗失之矣。

translations.literal: Confucius praised him, saying: "When he gained one good point, he held it firmly to his breast and never lost it."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius praised him, saying: "When he gained one good point, he clung to it close to his breast and never let it go."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「不遷怒，不貳過。

translations.literal: Again he said: "Do not transfer anger; do not repeat a fault."
translations.idiomatic: Again he said: "He did not transfer anger; he did not repeat a fault."

sentences.zh: 」「有不善未嘗不知，知之未嘗復行。

translations.literal: "When there was something not good, he never failed to know it; once he knew it, he never did it again."
translations.idiomatic: "When there was something not good, he never failed to know it; once he knew it, he never did it again."

sentences.zh: 」此其好之篤，學之得其道也。

translations.literal: This is the depth of his devotion; in learning he attained the correct Way.
translations.idiomatic: This was the depth of his devotion— in learning he had attained the correct Way.

sentences.zh: 然聖人則不思而得，不勉而中；

translations.literal: Now the sage obtains without thinking, hits the mark without striving;
translations.idiomatic: The sage obtains without thinking and hits the mark without striving;

sentences.zh: 顏子則必思而後得，必勉而後中。

translations.literal: Yanzi must think before obtaining, must strive before hitting the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzi had to think before obtaining and strive before hitting the mark.

sentences.zh: 其與聖人相去一息，所未至者守之也，非化之也。

translations.literal: His distance from the sage was but a single breath; what he had not yet reached was steadfast maintenance—not yet transformation.
translations.idiomatic: His distance from the sage was but a single breath; what he had not yet reached was steadfast maintenance, not yet transformation.

sentences.zh: 以其好學之心，假之以年，則不日而化矣。

translations.literal: With his heart devoted to learning, given years, he would in no time have been transformed.
translations.idiomatic: With his heart devoted to learning, given years, he would in no time have been transformed.

sentences.zh: 後人不達，以謂聖本生知，非學可至，而為學之道遂失。

translations.literal: Later people failed to understand, holding that sages are born knowing and that learning cannot reach them, and thus the Way of learning was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations failed to understand, holding that sages are born knowing and that learning cannot reach them— and so the Way of learning was lost.

sentences.zh: 不求諸己，而求諸外，以博聞強記、巧文麗辭為工，榮華其言，鮮有至於道者。

translations.literal: Not seeking within oneself but seeking without, taking broad learning, strong memory, clever writing, and elegant phrasing as craft, adorning their words with glory— few ever reached the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Not seeking within oneself but seeking without, they took broad learning, strong memory, clever writing, and elegant phrasing as their craft, adorning their words with glory— and few ever reached the Way.

sentences.zh: 則今之學，與顏子所好異矣。

translations.literal: Thus learning today differs from what Yanzi cherished.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the learning of today differs from what Yanzi cherished.

sentences.zh: 瑗得其文，大驚異之，即延見，處以學職。

translations.literal: Yuan obtained his essay and was greatly astonished, immediately invited him for an audience, and appointed him to an instructional post.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yuan obtained his essay and was greatly astonished; he immediately invited him for an audience and appointed him to an instructional post.

sentences.zh: 呂希哲首以師禮事頤。

translations.literal: Lü Xizhe was the first to serve Yi with the rites due a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Xizhe was the first to serve Cheng Yi with the rites due a teacher.

sentences.zh: 治平、元豐間，大臣屢薦，皆不起。

translations.literal: During the Zhiping and Yuanfeng eras, leading ministers repeatedly recommended him, yet he never accepted office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiping and Yuanfeng eras, leading ministers repeatedly recommended him, yet he never accepted office.

sentences.zh: 哲宗初，司馬光、呂公著共疏其行義曰：「伏見河南府處士程頤，力學好古，安貧守節，言必忠信，動遵禮法。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhezong's reign, Sima Guang and Lü Gongzhuo jointly memorialized regarding his conduct and righteousness, saying: "I respectfully observe the Henan Prefecture scholar Cheng Yi, who studies strenuously and loves antiquity, keeps poverty and holds to integrity, speaks always with loyalty and trustworthiness, and in action follows ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Zhezong's reign, Sima Guang and Lü Gongzhuo jointly memorialized regarding his conduct and righteousness, saying: "We respectfully observe the Henan Prefecture scholar Cheng Yi, who studies strenuously and loves antiquity, keeps poverty and holds to integrity, speaks always with loyalty and trustworthiness, and in action follows ritual and law.

sentences.zh: 年逾五十，不求仕進，真儒者之高蹈，聖世之逸民。

translations.literal: Over fifty years of age, he does not seek advancement in office—a true Confucian of lofty withdrawal, a recluse of the sage age.
translations.idiomatic: Past fifty years of age, he does not seek advancement in office— a true Confucian of lofty withdrawal, a recluse of this sage age.

sentences.zh: 望擢以不次，使士類有所矜式。

translations.literal: I hope he may be promoted out of turn, so that gentlemen may have one to emulate."
translations.idiomatic: We hope he may be promoted out of turn, so that gentlemen may have one to emulate."

sentences.zh: 」詔以為西京國子監教授，力辭。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Professor of the Western Capital Directorate of Education; he forcefully declined.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him Professor of the Western Capital Directorate of Education, but he forcefully declined.

sentences.zh: 尋召為秘書省校書郎，既入見，擢崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Proofreader in the Secretariat; after entering audience he was promoted to Lecturer at the Hall for the Promotion of Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as Proofreader in the Secretariat; after entering audience he was promoted to Lecturer at the Hall for the Promotion of Governance.

sentences.zh: 即上疏言：「習與智長，化與心成。

translations.literal: He immediately submitted a memorial saying: "Habit and wisdom grow together; transformation and the heart are accomplished together.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately submitted a memorial saying: "Habit and wisdom grow together; transformation and the heart are accomplished together.

sentences.zh: 今夫人民善教其子弟者，亦必延名德之士，使與之處，以薰陶成性。

translations.literal: Now when good common people teach their sons, they also surely invite men of renowned virtue to dwell with them, so as to cultivate and complete their nature through influence.
translations.idiomatic: When good common people teach their sons, they also surely invite men of renowned virtue to dwell with them, so as to cultivate and complete their nature through influence.

sentences.zh: 況陛下春秋之富，雖睿聖得於天資，而輔養之道不可不至。

translations.literal: Moreover your Majesty is in the springtime of youth; although sagely clarity comes from inborn talent, the Way of fostering and nurturing cannot but be carried to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Your Majesty is in the springtime of youth; although sagely clarity comes from inborn talent, the Way of fostering and nurturing cannot but be carried to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 大率一日之中，接賢士大夫之時多，親寺人宮女之時少，則氣質變化，自然而成。

translations.literal: In general, within a single day, if one meets eminent scholar-officials often and attends eunuchs and palace women rarely, then the native disposition is transformed and formed naturally.
translations.idiomatic: In general, within a single day, if one meets eminent scholar-officials often and attends eunuchs and palace women rarely, then the native disposition is transformed and formed naturally.

sentences.zh: 願選名儒入侍勸講，講罷留之分直，以備訪問，或有小失，隨事獻規，歲月積久，必能養成聖德。

translations.literal: I wish that eminent Confucians be selected to attend and lecture; after lecturing, some be kept on duty in rotation for consultation—or should there be a slight lapse, offer admonition on the spot—as the months and years accumulate, one will surely be able to cultivate sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: I wish that eminent Confucians be selected to attend and lecture; after lecturing, some be kept on duty in rotation for consultation—or should there be a slight lapse, offer admonition on the spot—as the months and years accumulate, one will surely be able to cultivate sagely virtue.

sentences.zh: 」頤每進講，色甚莊，繼以諷諫。

translations.literal: Whenever Yi entered to lecture, his demeanor was very solemn, followed by indirect admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Cheng Yi entered to lecture, his demeanor was very solemn, followed by indirect admonition.

sentences.zh: 聞帝在宮中盥而避蟻，問：「有是乎？

translations.literal: Hearing that the Emperor in the palace washed his face while avoiding ants, he asked: "Is it so?
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the Emperor in the palace washed his face while avoiding ants, he asked: "Is that so?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「然，誠恐傷之爾。

translations.literal: Yes—it was truly from fear of harming them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor answered: "Yes—it was truly from fear of harming them."

sentences.zh: 」頤曰：「推此心以及四海，帝王之要道也。」

translations.literal: Yi said: "Extend this heart to the four seas—this is the paramount Way of emperor and king."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi said: "Extend this heart to the four seas— this is the paramount Way of emperor and king."

sentences.zh: 神宗喪未除，冬至，百官表賀，頤言：「節序變遷，時思方切，乞改賀為慰。

translations.literal: Before the mourning for Shenzong was ended, at the winter solstice all officials submitted congratulatory memorials. Yi said: "As the seasons change, longing is especially keen— I beg that congratulation be changed to consolation.
translations.idiomatic: Before the mourning for Emperor Shenzong was ended, at the winter solstice all officials submitted congratulatory memorials. Cheng Yi said: "As the seasons change, longing is especially keen— I beg that congratulation be changed to consolation.

sentences.zh: 」既除喪，有司請開樂置宴，頤又言：「除喪而用吉禮，尚當因事張樂，今特設宴，是喜之也。

translations.literal: " After mourning ended, the relevant offices asked to open music and set a banquet. Yi again said: "When mourning ends and auspicious rites are used, music should still be arranged according to the occasion; now to set a special banquet is to rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended, the relevant offices asked to open music and set a banquet. Cheng Yi again said: "When mourning ends and auspicious rites are used, music should still be arranged according to the occasion; now to set a special banquet is to rejoice.

sentences.zh: 」皆從之。

translations.literal: All were followed.
translations.idiomatic: Both recommendations were followed.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗以瘡疹不禦邇英累日，頤詣宰相問安否，且曰：「上不禦殿，太后不當獨坐。

translations.literal: The Emperor once due to boils did not attend Ying Hall lectures for many days. Yi went to the chief councilor to inquire after his health, saying: "When the sovereign does not attend the hall, the Empress Dowager ought not sit alone.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once, due to boils, did not attend Ying Hall lectures for many days. Cheng Yi went to the chief councilor to inquire after his health, saying: "When the sovereign does not attend the hall, the Empress Dowager ought not sit alone.

sentences.zh: 且人主有疾，大臣可不知乎？

translations.literal: Moreover when the ruler is ill, can ministers not know?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover when the ruler is ill, can ministers not know?"

sentences.zh: 」翌日，宰相以下始奏請問疾。

translations.literal: The next day, the chief councilor and those below first memorialized requesting to inquire after his illness.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, the chief councilor and those below first memorialized requesting to inquire after his illness.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾不悅於頤，頤門人賈易、朱光庭不能平，合攻軾。

translations.literal: Su Shi bore ill will toward Yi; Yi's disciples Jia Yi and Zhu Guangting could not remain neutral and jointly attacked Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi bore ill will toward Cheng Yi; Yi's disciples Jia Yi and Zhu Guangting could not remain neutral and jointly attacked Su Shi.

sentences.zh: 胡宗愈、顧臨詆頤不宜用，孔文仲極論之，遂出管勾西京國子監。

translations.literal: Hu Zongyu and Gu Lin slandered Yi as unfit for appointment; Kong Wenzhong argued against him at length, and he was sent out as Supervisor of the Western Capital Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zongyu and Gu Lin slandered Cheng Yi as unfit for appointment; Kong Wenzhong argued against him at length, and he was sent out as Supervisor of the Western Capital Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 久之，加直秘閣，再上表辭。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was additionally granted Direct Appointment to the Secret Archives; he submitted a memorial twice declining.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time, he was additionally granted Direct Appointment to the Secret Archives; he submitted a memorial twice declining.

sentences.zh: 董敦逸復摭其有怨望語，去官。

translations.literal: Dong Dunyi again gathered his words of resentment and discontent; he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Dunyi again gathered his words of resentment and discontent, and he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，削籍竄涪州。

translations.literal: During the Shaosheng era, he was struck from the registers and banished to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaosheng era, he was struck from the registers and banished to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 李清臣尹洛，即日迫遣之，欲入別叔母亦不許，明日贐以銀百兩，頤不受。

translations.literal: Li Qingchen was prefect of Luoyang; that very day he pressed Yi to depart, and when Yi wished to enter to bid farewell to his aunt-mother he was not permitted; the next day Li sent one hundred taels of silver as a parting gift— Yi did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qingchen was prefect of Luoyang; that very day he pressed Cheng Yi to depart, and when Yi wished to enter to bid farewell to his aunt he was not permitted; the next day Li sent one hundred taels of silver as a parting gift— Yi did not accept.

sentences.zh: 徽宗即位，徙峽州，俄復其官，又奪于崇寧。

translations.literal: When Huizong took the throne, he was transferred to Xizhou; soon his office was restored, then again stripped during the Chongning era.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong took the throne, he was transferred to Xizhou; soon his office was restored, then again stripped during the Chongning era.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十五。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 頤於書無所不讀。

translations.literal: In books Yi read everything.
translations.idiomatic: There was no book Cheng Yi did not read.

sentences.zh: 其學本於誠，以《大學》、《語》、《孟》、《中庸》為標指，而達於《六經》。

translations.literal: His learning was rooted in sincerity, taking the Great Learning, Analects, Mencius, and Doctrine of the Mean as its guiding points, reaching through to the Six Classics.
translations.idiomatic: His learning was rooted in sincerity, taking the Great Learning, Analects, Mencius, and Doctrine of the Mean as its guiding points, and reaching through to the Six Classics.

sentences.zh: 動止語默，一以聖人為師，其不至乎聖人不止也。

translations.literal: In movement and stillness, speech and silence, he took the sage alone as teacher, and did not stop until he reached the sage.
translations.idiomatic: In movement and stillness, speech and silence, he took the sage alone as teacher, and did not stop until he reached the sage.

sentences.zh: 張載稱其兄弟從十四五時，便脫然欲學聖人，故卒得孔、孟不傳之學，以為諸儒倡。

translations.literal: Zhang Zai said that from the age of fourteen or fifteen the brothers abruptly wished to learn to become sages; thus in the end they obtained the learning of Confucius and Mencius that had not been transmitted, and became leaders among the Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zai said that from the age of fourteen or fifteen the Cheng brothers abruptly wished to learn to become sages; thus in the end they obtained the learning of Confucius and Mencius that had not been transmitted, and became leaders among the Confucians.

sentences.zh: 其言之旨，若布帛菽粟然，知德者尤尊崇之。

translations.literal: The purport of his words was like cloth, grain, beans, and millet; those who knew virtue especially honored him.
translations.idiomatic: The purport of his words was as plain as cloth, grain, beans, and millet; those who knew virtue especially honored him.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「今農夫祁寒暑雨，深耕易耨，播種五穀，吾得而食之；

translations.literal: Once he said: "Today's farmers, through cold and heat and pouring rain, deeply plow and frequently weed, sow the five grains—I obtain food thereby;
translations.idiomatic: Once he said: "Today's farmers, through cold and heat and pouring rain, deeply plow and frequently weed, sow the five grains—I obtain food thereby;

sentences.zh: 百工技藝，作為器物，吾得而用之；

translations.literal: Craftsmen of all trades fashion utensils—I obtain and use them;
translations.idiomatic: Craftsmen of all trades fashion utensils—I obtain and use them;

sentences.zh: 介胄之士，被堅執銳，以守土宇，吾得而安之。

translations.literal: Men in armor and helm, bearing strong shields and grasping sharp weapons, guard the realm—I obtain and dwell in peace thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Men in armor and helm, bearing strong shields and grasping sharp weapons, guard the realm—I obtain and dwell in peace thereby.

sentences.zh: 無功澤及人，而浪度歲月，晏然為天地間一蠹，唯綴緝聖人遺書，庶幾有補爾。

translations.literal: Without merit or bounty reaching others, yet passing the months in idleness, living at ease as a single parasite between Heaven and Earth— only by compiling and editing the sage's surviving books can one hope to be of some help.
translations.idiomatic: Without merit or bounty reaching others, yet passing the months in idleness, living at ease as a single parasite between Heaven and Earth— only by compiling and editing the sage's surviving books can one hope to be of some help.

sentences.zh: 」於是著《易》、《春秋傳》以傳於世。

translations.literal: Thus he authored commentaries on the Changes and Spring and Autumn Annals to transmit them to the world.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he authored commentaries on the Changes and Spring and Autumn Annals to transmit them to the world.

sentences.zh: 《易傳序》曰：

translations.literal: The Preface to the Commentary on the Changes says:
translations.idiomatic: The Preface to the Commentary on the Changes says:

sentences.zh: 《易》，變易也，隨時變易以從道也。

translations.literal: The Changes means change—changing in timely fashion to follow the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes means change— changing in timely fashion to follow the Way.

sentences.zh: 其為書也，廣大悉備，將以順性命之理，通幽明之故，盡事物之情，而示開物成務之道也。

translations.literal: As a book it is broad and complete in every part; it is meant to accord with the principles of nature and destiny, penetrate the reasons of darkness and light, exhaust the conditions of things, and reveal the Way of opening things and accomplishing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As a book it is broad and complete in every part; it is meant to accord with the principles of nature and destiny, penetrate the reasons of darkness and light, exhaust the conditions of things, and reveal the Way of opening things and accomplishing affairs.

sentences.zh: 聖人之憂患後世，可謂至矣。

translations.literal: The sage's solicitude for later generations may be called utmost.
translations.idiomatic: The sage's solicitude for later generations may be called utmost.

sentences.zh: 去古雖遠，遺經尚存，然而前儒失意以傳言，後學誦言而忘味，自秦而下，蓋無傳矣。

translations.literal: Though distant from antiquity, the transmitted classic still survives; yet earlier scholars lost the intent in transmitting words, later students recited words and forgot flavor; from Qin downward, broadly there was no transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Though distant from antiquity, the transmitted classic still survives; yet earlier scholars lost the intent in transmitting words, later students recited words and forgot flavor— from Qin downward, broadly there was no transmission.

sentences.zh: 予生千載之後，悼斯文之湮晦，將俾後人沿流而求源，此《傳》所以作也。

translations.literal: I was born after a thousand years, lamenting that this culture is buried in obscurity, wishing to let later people follow the stream to seek the source—this is why this Commentary was written.
translations.idiomatic: I was born after a thousand years, lamenting that this culture is buried in obscurity, wishing to let later people follow the stream to seek the source— this is why this Commentary was written.

sentences.zh: 「《易》有聖人之道四焉：以言者尚其辭，以動者尚其變，以制器者尚其象，以卜筮者尚其占」。

translations.literal: "The Changes has four aspects of the sage's Way: for those who speak, its words are honored; for those who act, its changes are honored; for those who make vessels, its images are honored; for those who divine, its prognostications are honored."
translations.idiomatic: "The Changes has four aspects of the sage's Way: for those who speak, its words are honored; for those who act, its changes are honored; for those who make vessels, its images are honored; for those who divine, its prognostications are honored."

sentences.zh: 吉凶消長之理、進退存亡之道備於辭，推辭考卦可以知變，象與占在其中矣。

translations.literal: The principles of fortune and misfortune, waning and waxing, the Way of advance and retreat, survival and extinction—all are complete in the words; by extrapolating from the words and examining the hexagrams one can know change; images and prognostications are within them.
translations.idiomatic: The principles of fortune and misfortune, waning and waxing, the Way of advance and retreat, survival and extinction—all are complete in the words; by extrapolating from the words and examining the hexagrams one can know change; images and prognostications are within them.

sentences.zh: 「君子居則觀其象而玩其辭，動則觀其變而玩其占」，得于辭不達其意者有矣，未有不得於辭而能通其意者也。

translations.literal: "When the noble person is at rest he observes the images and studies the words; when he acts he observes the changes and studies the prognostications"— there have been those who grasped the words yet did not reach the meaning, but none who failed to grasp the words yet could penetrate the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: "When the noble person is at rest he observes the images and studies the words; when he acts he observes the changes and studies the prognostications"— there have been those who grasped the words yet did not reach the meaning, but none who failed to grasp the words yet could penetrate the meaning.

sentences.zh: 至微者理也，至著者象也。

translations.literal: What is most subtle is principle; what is most manifest is image.
translations.idiomatic: What is most subtle is principle; what is most manifest is image.

sentences.zh: 體用一源，顯微無間，觀會通以行其典禮，則辭無所不備。

translations.literal: Substance and function have one source; the manifest and the subtle are without gap; observing where they meet and merge to practice their canonical rites— then the words are complete in every respect.
translations.idiomatic: Substance and function have one source; the manifest and the subtle are without gap; observing where they meet and merge to practice their canonical rites— then the words are complete in every respect.

sentences.zh: 故善學者，求言必自近，易於近者，非知言者也。

translations.literal: Therefore for one who learns well, seeking words must begin from what is near; those who find easy what is near are not those who know words.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore for one who learns well, seeking words must begin from what is near; those who find easy what is near are not those who know words.

sentences.zh: 予所傳者辭也，由辭以得意，則在乎人焉。

translations.literal: What I transmit are words; through words to grasp the meaning depends on the person.
translations.idiomatic: What I transmit are words; through words to grasp the meaning depends on the person.

sentences.zh: 《春秋傳序》曰：

translations.literal: The Preface to the Commentary on the Spring and Autumn says:
translations.idiomatic: The Preface to the Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says:

sentences.zh: 天之生民，必有出類之才起而君長之，治之而爭奪息，導之而生養遂，教之而倫理明，然後人道立，天道成，地道平。

translations.literal: Heaven in producing the people must surely raise outstanding talent to lead and rule them, govern them so that struggle and seizure cease, guide them so that nurture and sustenance prosper, teach them so that human relations are clarified— then the human Way is established, the heavenly Way is accomplished, and the earthly Way is leveled.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven in producing the people must surely raise outstanding talent to lead and rule them, govern them so that struggle and seizure cease, guide them so that nurture and sustenance prosper, teach them so that human relations are clarified— then the human Way is established, the heavenly Way is accomplished, and the earthly Way is leveled.

sentences.zh: 二帝而上，聖賢世出，隨時有作，順乎風氣之宜，不先天以開人，各因時而立政。

translations.literal: Above the Two Emperors, sages and worthies emerged generation after generation, acting according to the times, following the suitability of the prevailing ethos—not anticipating Heaven to open men's minds, each establishing government according to the time.
translations.idiomatic: Above the Two Emperors, sages and worthies emerged generation after generation, acting according to the times, following the suitability of the prevailing ethos— not anticipating Heaven to open men's minds, each establishing government according to the time.

sentences.zh: 暨乎三王迭興，三重既備，子、丑、寅之建正，忠、質、文之更尚，人道備矣，天運周矣。

translations.literal: When the Three Kings rose in turn, the threefold system was complete; the first months established in zi, chou, and yin; loyalty, simplicity, and refinement alternately honored— the human Way was complete and Heaven's cycle was full.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Kings rose in turn, the threefold system was complete; the first months established in zi, chou, and yin; loyalty, simplicity, and refinement alternately honored— the human Way was complete and Heaven's cycle was full.

sentences.zh: 聖王既不復作，有天下者雖欲仿古之跡，亦私意妄為而已。

translations.literal: Once sage kings no longer arose, those who possessed the realm, though wishing to imitate the traces of antiquity, did so by private whim and reckless action only.
translations.idiomatic: Once sage kings no longer arose, those who possessed the realm, though wishing to imitate the traces of antiquity, did so by private whim and reckless action only.

sentences.zh: 事之繆，秦至以建亥為正；

translations.literal: In the confusion of affairs, Qin even took the tenth month as the first month;
translations.idiomatic: In the confusion of affairs, Qin even took the tenth month as the first month;

sentences.zh: 道之悖，漢專以智力持世，豈復知先王之道也。

translations.literal: In the perversion of the Way, Han relied solely on wit and force to hold the world— how could they still know the Way of the former kings?
translations.idiomatic: In the perversion of the Way, Han relied solely on wit and force to hold the world— how could they still know the Way of the former kings?

sentences.zh: 夫子當周之末，以聖人不復作也，順天應時之治不復有也，於是作《春秋》，為百王不易之大法。

translations.literal: When the Master stood at the end of Zhou, because sage men no longer arose and governance in accord with Heaven and the times no longer existed, he therefore composed the Spring and Autumn Annals as the great method unchanging for a hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: When the Master stood at the end of Zhou, because sage men no longer arose and governance in accord with Heaven and the times no longer existed, he therefore composed the Spring and Autumn Annals as the great method unchanging for a hundred kings.

sentences.zh: 所謂「考諸三王而不繆，建諸天地而不悖，質諸鬼神而無疑，百世以俟聖人而不惑」者也。

translations.literal: What is called "examined against the Three Kings without error, established against Heaven and Earth without perversity, tested against ghosts and spirits without doubt, awaiting a sage for a hundred generations without confusion."
translations.idiomatic: What is called "examined against the Three Kings without error, established against Heaven and Earth without perversity, tested against ghosts and spirits without doubt, awaiting a sage for a hundred generations without confusion."

sentences.zh: 先儒之傳，游、夏不能贊一辭，辭不待贊者也，言不能與於斯爾。

translations.literal: The transmission of earlier scholars— Ziyou and Xia could not add a single word; words need no praise, for speech cannot enter this realm.
translations.idiomatic: The transmission of earlier scholars— Ziyou and Xia could not add a single word; words need no praise, for speech cannot enter this realm.

sentences.zh: 斯道也，唯顏子嘗聞之矣。

translations.literal: This Way— only Yanzi once heard it.
translations.idiomatic: This Way— only Yanzi once heard it.

sentences.zh: 「行夏之時，乘殷之輅，服周之冕，樂則《韶舞》，此其准的也。

translations.literal: "Use the calendar of Xia, ride the chariots of Yin, wear the ceremonial caps of Zhou, and for music the Shao dance"— this is its mark.
translations.idiomatic: "Use the calendar of Xia, ride the chariots of Yin, wear the ceremonial caps of Zhou, and for music the Shao dance"— this is its mark.

sentences.zh: 後史以吏視《春秋》，謂褒善貶惡而已，至於經世之大法，則不知也。

translations.literal: Later historians viewed the Spring and Autumn as a clerk would, saying it merely rewards good and punishes evil— as for the great methods of governing the age, they did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Later historians viewed the Spring and Autumn as a clerk would, saying it merely rewards good and punishes evil— as for the great methods of governing the age, they did not know.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》大義數十，其義雖大，炳如日星，乃易見也。

translations.literal: The great principles of the Spring and Autumn are several tens; though the principles are great, they are as bright as the sun and stars— easy to see.
translations.idiomatic: The great principles of the Spring and Autumn are several tens; though the principles are great, they are as bright as the sun and stars— easy to see.

sentences.zh: 惟其微辭隱義、時措從宜者，為難知也。

translations.literal: Only its subtle words, hidden meanings, and timely adjustments according to circumstances are hard to know.
translations.idiomatic: Only its subtle words, hidden meanings, and timely adjustments according to circumstances are hard to know.

sentences.zh: 或抑或縱，或予或奪，或進或退，或微或顯，而得乎義理之安，文質之中，寬猛之宜，是非之公，乃制事之權衡，揆道之模範也。

translations.literal: Now restraining or releasing, granting or taking away, advancing or retreating, subtle or manifest—and yet attaining the security of principle and meaning, the balance of substance and refinement, the fitness of leniency and severity, the fairness of right and wrong— these are the balance of determining affairs and the model for measuring the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Whether restraining or releasing, granting or taking away, advancing or retreating, subtle or manifest— and yet attaining the security of principle and meaning, the balance of substance and refinement, the fitness of leniency and severity, the fairness of right and wrong— these are the balance of determining affairs and the model for measuring the Way.

sentences.zh: 夫觀百物然後識化工之神，聚眾材然後知作室之用，於一事一義而欲窺聖人之用心，非上智不能也。

translations.literal: One must observe a hundred things before one recognizes the divine craft of nature; one must gather many materials before one knows the use of building a house—to wish from a single affair or a single principle to glimpse the sage's intent is not within the reach of any but the highest wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: One must observe a hundred things before one recognizes the divine craft of nature; one must gather many materials before one knows the use of building a house— to wish from a single affair or a single principle to glimpse the sage's intent is not within the reach of any but the highest wisdom.

sentences.zh: 故學《春秋》者，必優遊涵泳，默識心通，然後能造其微也。

translations.literal: Therefore those who study the Spring and Autumn must leisurely wade and immerse, silently recognizing until the heart penetrates— only then can they reach its subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore those who study the Spring and Autumn must leisurely wade and immerse, silently recognizing until the heart penetrates— only then can they reach its subtlety.

sentences.zh: 後王知《春秋》之義，則雖德非禹、湯，尚可以法三代之治。

translations.literal: If later kings knew the meaning of the Spring and Autumn, then though their virtue fell short of Yu and Tang, they could still model the governance of the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: If later kings knew the meaning of the Spring and Autumn, then though their virtue fell short of Yu and Tang, they could still model the governance of the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 自秦而下，其學不傳，予悼夫聖人之志不明於後世也，故作《傳》以明之，俾後之人通其文而求其義，得其意而法其用，則三代可復也。

translations.literal: From Qin downward its learning was not transmitted; I lament that the sage's intent is unclear to later generations; therefore I composed this Commentary to clarify it, enabling later people to penetrate its text and seek its meaning, grasp its intent and model its application— then the Three Dynasties can be restored.
translations.idiomatic: From Qin downward its learning was not transmitted; I lament that the sage's intent is unclear to later generations; therefore I composed this Commentary to clarify it, enabling later people to penetrate its text and seek its meaning, grasp its intent and model its application— then the Three Dynasties can be restored.

sentences.zh: 是《傳》也，雖未能極聖人之蘊奧，庶幾學者得其門而入矣。

translations.literal: This Commentary— though it cannot fully exhaust the sage's hidden depths, may yet enable scholars to find the door and enter.
translations.idiomatic: This Commentary cannot fully plumb the sage's hidden depths, yet it may still enable scholars to find the door and enter.

sentences.zh: 平生誨人不倦，故學者出其門最多，淵源所漸，皆為名士。

translations.literal: Throughout his life he instructed others without weariness; thus of scholars who passed through his gate there were the most, and those whom his influence gradually reached all became eminent men.
translations.idiomatic: He taught tirelessly all his life, and more students passed through his gate than through any other; those touched by his influence in turn all became men of note.

sentences.zh: 涪人祠頤於北岩，世稱為伊川先生。

translations.literal: The people of Fu erected a shrine to Yi at North Cliff; the age knows him as Master Yichuan.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fu built a shrine to Cheng Yi at North Cliff, and the age knows him as Master Yichuan.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十三年，賜諡曰正公。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiading, he was granted the posthumous title Lord Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Jiading, he was granted the posthumous title Lord Zheng.

sentences.zh: 淳祐元年，封伊陽伯，從祀孔子廟庭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunyou, he was enfeoffed as Earl of Yiyang and granted attendance at sacrificial rites in Confucius's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chunyou, he was enfeoffed as Earl of Yiyang and granted a place in the sacrificial rites at Confucius's temple.

sentences.zh: 門人劉絢、李籲、謝良佐、游酢、張繹、蘇昞皆班班可書，附于左。

translations.literal: His disciples Liu Xu, Li Na, Xie Liangzuo, You Zuo, Zhang Yi, and Su Bing were each worthy of record; they are appended below.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples Liu Xu, Li Na, Xie Liangzuo, You Zuo, Zhang Yi, and Su Bing were each worthy of record and are appended below.

sentences.zh: 呂大鈞、大臨見《大防傳》。

translations.literal: Lü Dajun and Dalin are treated in the Biography of Da Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dajun and Lü Dalin are treated in the Biography of Lü Dafang.

sentences.zh: 張載，字子厚，長安人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zai, courtesy name Zihou, was a native of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zai, styled Zihou, was a native of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 少喜談兵。

translations.literal: In youth he delighted in discussing warfare.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he delighted in discussing military affairs.

sentences.zh: 至欲結客取洮西之地。

translations.literal: He even wished to gather followers and seize the lands west of the Tao River.
translations.idiomatic: He even wished to gather companions and seize the lands west of the Tao River.

sentences.zh: 年二十一，以書謁范仲淹，一見知其遠器，乃警之曰：「儒者自有名教可樂，何事於兵。

translations.literal: At twenty-one he sent a letter to visit Fan Zhongyan; at first sight Fan perceived his far-reaching capacity and warned him, saying: "The Confucian has the delights of moral teaching— what need is there for military affairs?
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-one he sent a letter to Fan Zhongyan; at first meeting Fan perceived his great promise and admonished him: "The Confucian has the delights of moral teaching— why turn to arms?

sentences.zh: 」因勸讀《中庸》。

translations.literal: " He therefore urged him to read the Doctrine of the Mean.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore urged him to read the Doctrine of the Mean.

sentences.zh: 載讀其書，猶以為未足，又訪諸釋、老，累年究極其說，知無所得，反而求之《六經》。

translations.literal: Zai read the work yet still found it insufficient; he then sought instruction from Buddhist and Daoist teachers, and for years pursued their doctrines to the limit, knowing he had gained nothing, and turned back to seek in the Six Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zai read it but still found it insufficient; he then sought out Buddhist and Daoist teachers and for years pursued their doctrines to the end, knowing he had gained nothing, and turned back to the Six Classics.

sentences.zh: 嘗坐虎皮講《易》京師，聽從者甚眾。

translations.literal: Once he sat upon a tiger skin and lectured on the Changes in the capital, and those who came to listen were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Once he sat on a tiger skin and lectured on the Changes in the capital, and the audience was very large.

sentences.zh: 一夕，二程至，與論《易》，次日語人曰：「比見二程，深明《易》道，吾所弗及，汝輩可師之。

translations.literal: One evening the two Chengs arrived; they debated the Changes with him, and the next day he told people: "Having now met the two Chengs, who deeply understand the Way of the Changes— I cannot match them; you should take them as your teachers.
translations.idiomatic: One evening the two Cheng brothers came and debated the Changes with him; the next day he told his listeners: "Now that I have met the two Chengs, who deeply understand the Way of the Changes, I cannot match them— you should take them as your teachers.

sentences.zh: 」撤坐輟講。

translations.literal: " He dismantled his seat and ceased lecturing.
translations.idiomatic: He dismantled his seat and stopped lecturing.

sentences.zh: 與二程語道學之要，渙然自信曰：「吾道自足，何事旁求。

translations.literal: Speaking with the two Chengs on the essentials of the Learning of the Way, he was suddenly confident and said: "My Way is self-sufficient— what need to seek elsewhere?
translations.idiomatic: In conversation with the two Chengs on the essentials of the Learning of the Way, he was suddenly confident and said: "My Way is complete in itself— why seek elsewhere?

sentences.zh: 」於是盡棄異學，淳如也。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he wholly abandoned heterodox learning, pure and clear as before.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he wholly abandoned heterodox learning and became pure and clear in his purpose.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為祈州司法參軍，雲岩令。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as judicial assistant of Qizhou and magistrate of Yuyan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as judicial assistant of Qizhou and magistrate of Yuyan.

sentences.zh: 政事以敦本善俗為先，每月吉，具酒食，召鄉人高年會縣庭，親為勸酬。

translations.literal: In governance he put first strengthening foundations and improving customs; on each auspicious day of the month he prepared wine and food, summoned elderly villagers to gather in the county hall, and personally urged toasts upon them.
translations.idiomatic: In office he put strengthening foundations and improving customs first; on each auspicious day of the month he prepared wine and food, summoned the village elders to the county hall, and personally urged toasts upon them.

sentences.zh: 使人知養老事長之義，因問民疾苦，及告所以訓戒子弟之意。

translations.literal: He made people understand the principle of nourishing the aged and serving elders; meanwhile he inquired into the people's hardships and announced his intent in instructing and warning the younger generation.
translations.idiomatic: He taught people the duty of caring for the aged and honoring elders, inquired into their hardships, and explained how he meant to instruct and warn the young.

sentences.zh: 熙甯初，御史中丞呂公著言其有古學，神宗方一新百度，思得才哲士謀之，召見問治道，對曰：「為政不法三代者，終苟道也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xining era, Censor-in-Chief Lü Gongzhu said he possessed ancient learning; Emperor Shenzong was at that time renewing all institutions and wished to obtain talented and wise men to consult; he summoned Zhang and asked about the way of governance, and Zhang replied: "Whoever governs without taking the Three Dynasties as his model ends in a flippant and shallow path.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xining era, Censor-in-Chief Lü Gongzhu reported that Zhang Zai possessed ancient learning; Emperor Shenzong was then renewing all institutions and sought talented and wise counselors; he summoned Zhang and asked about governance, and Zhang replied: "Whoever governs without taking the Three Dynasties as his model ends on a shallow and careless path.

sentences.zh: 」帝悅，以為崇文院校書。

translations.literal: " The emperor was pleased and appointed him collator at the Chongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and appointed him collator at the Chongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 他日見王安石，安石問以新政，載曰：「公與人為善，則人以善歸公；

translations.literal: On another day he saw Wang Anshi; Anshi inquired about the New Policies, and Zai said: "If you do good for others, then people will attribute goodness to you;
translations.idiomatic: On another day he met Wang Anshi, who asked about the New Policies; Zhang Zai said: "If you do good for others, people will return goodness to you;

sentences.zh: 如教玉人琢玉，則宜有不受命者矣。

translations.literal: but as when instructing a jade worker to carve jade— there ought to be those who do not accept the commission.
translations.idiomatic: but as when one instructs a jade carver to cut jade, there will be those who refuse the command.

sentences.zh: 」明州苗振獄起，往治之，末殺其罪。

translations.literal: " When the Miao Zhen case arose in Mingzhou, he was sent to try it and in the end did not apply the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: When the Miao Zhen case arose in Mingzhou, he was sent to try it and in the end did not impose the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 還朝，即移疾屏居南山下，終日危坐一室，左右簡編，俯而讀，仰而思，有得則識之，或中夜起坐，取燭以書。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he immediately cited illness and retired to live sequestered at the foot of South Mountain; all day he sat upright in one room, books piled on either side— reading with head bowed, thinking with head raised; when he gained something he wrote it down, and sometimes at midnight he would rise, take a candle, and compose.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to court, he immediately pleaded illness and withdrew to live in seclusion at the foot of South Mountain; all day he sat upright in one room with books on either side— reading with head bowed, thinking with head raised; when he gained insight he wrote it down, and sometimes at midnight he would rise, take a candle, and write.

sentences.zh: 其志道精思，未始須臾息，亦未嘗須臾忘也。

translations.literal: His intent to pursue the Way and his penetrating thought never ceased for an instant, nor was ever forgotten for an instant.
translations.idiomatic: His resolve to pursue the Way and his penetrating thought never ceased for an instant, nor was ever forgotten for an instant.

sentences.zh: 敝衣蔬食，與諸生講學，每告以知禮成性、變化氣質之道，學必如聖人而後已。

translations.literal: Wearing shabby clothes and eating plain food, he lectured with his students, always teaching them the way of knowing ritual to complete one's nature and transforming one's temperament— learning must not cease until one is like a sage.
translations.idiomatic: In shabby clothes and plain food he lectured to his students, always teaching them how knowing ritual completes one's nature and how temperament may be transformed— study must not cease until one becomes like a sage.

sentences.zh: 以為知人而不知天，求為賢人而不求為聖人，此秦、漢以來學者大蔽也。

translations.literal: He held that to know human affairs but not Heaven, to seek to become a worthy but not a sage— this was the great blindness of scholars since Qin and Han.
translations.idiomatic: He held that to know human affairs but not Heaven, to seek to become a worthy but not a sage— this was the great blindness of scholars since Qin and Han.

sentences.zh: 故其學尊禮貴德、樂天安命，以《易》為宗，以《中庸》為體，以《孔》、《孟》為法，黜怪妄，辨鬼神。

translations.literal: Thus his learning honored ritual and valued virtue, rejoiced in Heaven and accepted fate; he took the Changes as his foundation, the Doctrine of the Mean as his substance, the Analects and Mencius as his standard; he repudiated the bizarre and absurd and distinguished the nature of ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Thus his learning honored ritual and valued virtue, rejoiced in Heaven and accepted fate; he took the Changes as his foundation, the Doctrine of the Mean as his substance, the Analects and Mencius as his model; he repudiated the bizarre and absurd and clarified the nature of ghosts and spirits.

sentences.zh: 其家昏喪葬祭，率用先王之意，而傅以今禮。

translations.literal: In his household, weddings, funerals, burials, and sacrifices generally followed the intent of the ancient kings, adapted with present-day ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In his household, weddings, funerals, burials, and sacrifices generally followed the intent of the ancient kings, adapted with present-day ritual forms.

sentences.zh: 又論定井田、宅裏、發斂、學校之法，皆欲條理成書，使可舉而措諸事業。

translations.literal: He also discussed and fixed methods for the well-field system, residential districts, revenue collection, and schools, all wishing to arrange them into coherent books so they could be lifted up and applied in actual undertakings.
translations.idiomatic: He also worked out methods for the well-field system, residential districts, revenue collection, and schools, intending to arrange them into coherent books that could be taken up and put into practice.

sentences.zh: 呂大防薦之曰：「載之始終，善發明聖人之遺旨，其論政治略可復古。

translations.literal: Lü Dafang recommended him, saying: "From beginning to end, Zai excels at elucidating the sages' transmitted intent; his discussions of governance can largely restore antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dafang recommended him, saying: "From first to last, Zhang Zai excels at elucidating the sages' transmitted intent; his discussions of governance can largely restore antiquity.

sentences.zh: 宜還其舊職，以備諮訪。

translations.literal: He ought to be restored to his former office to be available for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: He ought to be restored to his former office and made available for consultation.

sentences.zh: 」乃詔知太常禮院。

translations.literal: " An edict then made him director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then appointed him director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 與有司議禮不合，復以疾歸，中道疾甚，沐浴更衣而寢，旦而卒。

translations.literal: His discussions of ritual with the relevant offices did not accord; again citing illness he returned home; on the way his illness grew severe; he bathed, changed his clothes, and lay down, and at dawn he died.
translations.idiomatic: His discussions of ritual with the relevant offices did not agree; again pleading illness he returned home; on the way his illness grew severe; he bathed, changed his clothes, and lay down, and at dawn he died.

sentences.zh: 貧無以斂，門人共買棺奉其喪還。

translations.literal: So poor that there were no means for the burial, his disciples jointly purchased a coffin and conducted his funeral home.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to afford a burial, his disciples jointly purchased a coffin and escorted his body home.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士許將等言其恬於進取，乞加贈恤，詔賜館職半賻。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Xu Jiang and others said he was content and indifferent to advancement, and asked that additional posthumous honors and compensation be granted; an edict granted him half the usual funeral stipend for an academician post.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Xu Jiang and others said he was indifferent to advancement and asked that additional posthumous honors be granted; an edict awarded him half the usual funeral stipend for an academician post.

sentences.zh: 載學古力行，為關中士人宗師，世稱為橫渠先生。

translations.literal: Zai studied antiquity and practiced earnestly, becoming the master and exemplar of scholars in the Guanzhong region; the age knows him as Master Hengqu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zai studied antiquity and practiced earnestly, becoming the master and exemplar of scholars in the Guanzhong region; the age knows him as Master Hengqu.

sentences.zh: 著書號《正蒙》，又作《西銘》曰：

translations.literal: He composed a work entitled Correcting Obscurantism, and also wrote the Western Inscription, which says:
translations.idiomatic: He composed a work entitled Correcting Obscurantism, and also wrote the Western Inscription, which says:

sentences.zh: 乾稱父而坤母，予茲藐焉，乃混然中處。

translations.literal: Heaven is my father and Earth my mother, and of all that fills them I am the tiniest, yet I dwell in their midst undifferentiated.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is my father and Earth my mother, and of all that fills them I am the tiniest, yet I dwell in their midst undifferentiated.

sentences.zh: 故天地之塞吾其體，天地之帥吾其性，民吾同胞，物吾與也。

translations.literal: Therefore that which fills Heaven and Earth is my body, that which leads Heaven and Earth is my nature; the people are my brethren, and all things are my companions.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore that which fills Heaven and Earth is my body, that which leads Heaven and Earth is my nature; the people are my brethren, and all things are my companions.

sentences.zh: 大君者，吾父母宗子；

translations.literal: The great ruler is the eldest son of our parents;
translations.idiomatic: The great ruler is the eldest son of our parents;

sentences.zh: 其大臣，宗子之家相也。

translations.literal: his great ministers are the house steward of that eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: his great ministers are the house steward of that eldest son.

sentences.zh: 尊高年所以長其長，慈孤幼所以幼其幼，聖其合德，賢其秀也。

translations.literal: Honoring the aged is thus to honor their elders; cherishing the orphaned young is thus to cherish their young; the sage joins virtue together; the worthy is outstanding among the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring the aged is thus to honor their elders; cherishing the orphaned young is thus to cherish their young; the sage joins virtue together; the worthy stands out among the rest.

sentences.zh: 凡天下疲癃殘疾、恂獨鰥寡，皆吾兄弟之顛連而無告者也。

translations.literal: All throughout the realm— the feeble, the crippled, the maimed, the solitary and alone, widows and orphans— are my brothers who wander in distress with none to tell their woes.
translations.idiomatic: All throughout the realm— the feeble, the crippled, the maimed, the solitary and alone, widows and orphans— are my brothers who wander in distress with none to tell their woes.

sentences.zh: 「于時保之」，子之翼也。

translations.literal: "Preserving them in their hour"— this is a son's sheltering wing.
translations.idiomatic: "Preserving them in their hour"— this is a son's sheltering wing.

sentences.zh: 「樂且不憂」，純乎孝者也。

translations.literal: "Joy without sorrow"— this is perfect filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: "Joy without sorrow"— this is perfect filial piety.

sentences.zh: 違曰悖德，害仁曰賊，濟惡者不才，其踐形惟肖者也。

translations.literal: To oppose is called transgressing virtue; to harm the humane is called being a robber; to abet evil is to be without talent; only one who fully embodies form resembles the ideal.
translations.idiomatic: To oppose is called transgressing virtue; to harm the humane is called being a robber; to abet evil is to be without talent; only one who fully embodies form resembles the ideal.

sentences.zh: 知化則善述其事，窮神則善繼其志，不愧屋漏為無忝，存心養性為匪懈。

translations.literal: Knowing transformation is to well continue one's affairs; penetrating spirit is to well carry on one's aim; to be without shame before one who watches unseen is to be without disgrace; to preserve the heart and nourish nature is to be without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing transformation is to well continue one's affairs; penetrating spirit is to well carry on one's aim; to be without shame before one who watches unseen is to be without disgrace; to preserve the heart and nourish nature is to be without slackening.

sentences.zh: 惡旨酒，崇伯之子顧養；

translations.literal: To loathe strong drink— this is the attentive nurturing of Chongbo's son;
translations.idiomatic: To loathe strong drink— this is the attentive nurturing of Chongbo's son;

sentences.zh: 育英材，潁封人之錫類。

translations.literal: To nurture outstanding talent— this is the Lord of Ying's extending grace to his kind;
translations.idiomatic: To nurture outstanding talent— this is the Lord of Ying's extending grace to his kind;

sentences.zh: 不弛勞而底豫，舜其功也；

translations.literal: Not slackening in toil yet bringing delight— this was Shun's achievement;
translations.idiomatic: Not slackening in toil yet bringing delight— this was Shun's achievement;

sentences.zh: 無所逃而待烹，申生其恭也。

translations.literal: Having nowhere to flee yet awaiting execution— this was Shensheng's reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Having nowhere to flee yet awaiting execution— this was Shensheng's reverence.

sentences.zh: 體其受而歸全者，參乎；

translations.literal: Embodying what one receives and returning it whole— was this not Zeng Shen?
translations.idiomatic: Embodying what one receives and returning it whole— was this not Zeng Shen?

sentences.zh: 勇於從而順令者，伯奇也。

translations.literal: Bearing courage in obedience and following the command— was this not Boqi?
translations.idiomatic: Bearing courage in obedience and following the command— was this not Boqi?

sentences.zh: 富貴福澤，將厚吾之生也；

translations.literal: Wealth, honor, good fortune, and blessing will enrich my life;
translations.idiomatic: Wealth, honor, good fortune, and blessing will enrich my life;

sentences.zh: 貧賤憂戚，庸玉女于成也。

translations.literal: Poverty, low estate, sorrow, and distress will temper and refine my accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: Poverty, low estate, sorrow, and distress will temper and refine my person to completion.

sentences.zh: 存，吾順事；

translations.literal: While I live, I follow my duties;
translations.idiomatic: While I live, I follow my duties;

sentences.zh: 歿，吾寧也。

translations.literal: When I die, I am at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When I die, I am at peace.

sentences.zh: 程頤嘗言：「《西銘》明理一而分殊，擴前聖所未發，與孟子性善養氣之論同功，自孟子後蓋未之見。

translations.literal: Cheng Yi once said: "The Western Inscription clarifies that principle is one while its manifestations are diverse; it expands on what prior sages had not yet brought forth. It shares the same achievement as Mencius's doctrine of the goodness of human nature and the nurturing of vital energy; since Mencius there has likely been nothing like it.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi once said: "The Western Inscription clarifies that principle is one while its particular manifestations are many; it expands on what prior sages had not yet brought forth. It shares the same achievement as Mencius's doctrine of the goodness of human nature and the nurturing of vital energy; since Mencius there has likely been nothing like it.

sentences.zh: 」學者至今尊其書。

translations.literal: " Scholars to this day honor his book.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars to this day honor his book.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十三年，賜諡曰明公。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiading, he was granted the posthumous title Lord Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Jiading, he was granted the posthumous title Lord Ming.

sentences.zh: 淳祐元年封郿伯，從祀孔子廟庭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunyou he was enfeoffed as Earl of Mei and granted attendance at sacrificial rites in Confucius's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chunyou he was enfeoffed as Earl of Mei and granted a place in the sacrificial rites at Confucius's temple.

sentences.zh: 弟戩。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Jian.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Jian.

sentences.zh: 弟 戩

translations.literal: Younger brother: Jian
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Jian

sentences.zh: 戩，字天祺。

translations.literal: Jian, courtesy name Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, styled Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 起進士，調閿鄉主簿，知金堂縣。

translations.literal: He rose through the jinshi examination, was appointed chief clerk of Wenxiang, and served as magistrate of Jintang County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed chief clerk of Wenxiang, and served as magistrate of Jintang County.

sentences.zh: 誠心愛人，養老恤窮，間召父老使教督子弟。

translations.literal: He sincerely loved people, cared for the aged and comforted the destitute, and from time to time summoned elders to instruct and supervise the younger generation.
translations.idiomatic: He sincerely loved the people, cared for the aged and comforted the destitute, and from time to time summoned elders to instruct and supervise the young.

sentences.zh: 民有小善，皆籍記之。

translations.literal: When the people performed small acts of goodness, he recorded them all.
translations.idiomatic: When the people performed small acts of goodness, he recorded them all.

sentences.zh: 以奉錢為酒食，月吉，召老者飲勞，使其子孫侍，勸以孝弟。

translations.literal: Using his salary he prepared wine and food; on auspicious days of the month he summoned the aged to drink and be refreshed, had their descendants wait upon them, and urged filial piety and brotherly respect.
translations.idiomatic: Using his salary he prepared wine and food; on auspicious days of the month he summoned the aged to drink and be refreshed, had their descendants wait upon them, and urged filial piety and brotherly respect.

sentences.zh: 民化其德，所至獄訟日少。

translations.literal: The people were transformed by his virtue; wherever he served, lawsuits grew fewer day by day.
translations.idiomatic: The people were transformed by his virtue; wherever he served, lawsuits grew fewer day by day.

sentences.zh: 熙甯初，為監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xining era, he served as supervising censor in a probationary capacity.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xining era, he served as supervising censor in a probationary capacity.

sentences.zh: 累章論王安石亂法，乞罷條例司及追還常平使者。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized that Wang Anshi was disrupting the laws, and begged that the Commission for Policies be abolished and the grain-transport commissioners recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized that Wang Anshi was disrupting the laws and begged that the Commission for Policies be abolished and the grain-transport commissioners recalled.

sentences.zh: 劾曾公亮、陳升之、趙抃依違不能救正，韓絳左右徇從，與為死黨，李定以邪諂竊台諫。

translations.literal: He impeached Zeng Gongliang, Chen Shengzhi, and Zhao Bian for waffling and failing to set things right; Han Jiang for catering to Wang on either side and becoming his diehard faction; and Li Ding for usurping a censor's post through flattery and wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Zeng Gongliang, Chen Shengzhi, and Zhao Bian for waffling and failing to set things right; Han Jiang for catering to Wang on either side and becoming his diehard faction; and Li Ding for usurping a censor's post through flattery and wickedness.

sentences.zh: 且安石擅國，輔以絳之詭隨，台臣又用定輩，繼續而來，芽蘖漸盛。

translations.literal: Moreover Wang Anshi monopolized the state, assisted by Han Jiang's slick compliance; censorial officials employed men like Li Ding; one after another they came, and new shoots gradually flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Wang Anshi monopolized the state, assisted by Han Jiang's slick compliance; censorial officials employed men like Li Ding; one after another they came, and new shoots gradually flourished.

sentences.zh: 呂惠卿劾薄辯給，假經術以文奸言，豈宜勸講君側。

translations.literal: Lü Huiqing's impeachments were shallow yet glib; he used classical learning to adorn wicked words— how could he be fit to counsel the ruler at his side?
translations.idiomatic: Lü Huiqing's impeachments were shallow yet glib; he used classical learning to adorn wicked words— how could he be fit to counsel the ruler at his side?

sentences.zh: 書數十上，又詣中書爭之，安石舉扇掩面而笑，戩曰：「戩之狂直宜為公笑，然天下之笑公者不少矣。

translations.literal: He submitted dozens of memorials and also went to the Secretariat to dispute the matter; Wang Anshi raised his fan to cover his face and laughed. Jian said: "My rash directness is fit matter for you to laugh at— yet those throughout the realm who laugh at you are not few.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted dozens of memorials and also went to the Secretariat to dispute the matter; Wang Anshi raised his fan to cover his face and laughed. Jian said: "My rash directness is fit matter for you to laugh at— yet those throughout the realm who laugh at you are not few.

sentences.zh: 」趙抃從旁解之，戩曰：「公亦不得為無罪。

translations.literal: " Zhao Bian interceded from the side; Jian said: "You too cannot be held guiltless.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bian interceded from the side; Jian said: "You too cannot be held guiltless.

sentences.zh: 」抃有愧色。

translations.literal: " Zhao showed a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao showed a look of shame.

sentences.zh: 遂稱病待罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon he pleaded illness and awaited punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he pleaded illness and awaited punishment.

sentences.zh: 出知公安縣，徙監司竹監，至舉家不食筍。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Gong'an County, then transferred to supervise the bamboo plantation— so thoroughly that his entire household ceased eating bamboo shoots.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Gong'an County, then transferred to supervise the bamboo plantation— so thoroughly that his entire household ceased eating bamboo shoots.

sentences.zh: 常愛用一卒，及將代，自見其人盜筍籜，治之無少貸；

translations.literal: He once favored employing one soldier; when the time came for his replacement, he personally saw the man stealing bamboo sheaths and punished him without the slightest lenience;
translations.idiomatic: He once favored employing one soldier; when the time came for his replacement, he personally saw the man stealing bamboo sheaths and punished him without the slightest lenience;

sentences.zh: 罪已正，待之復如初，略不介意，其德量如此。

translations.literal: once the penalty was exacted, he treated the man again as before, not minding in the least— such was his moral capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Once the penalty was exacted, he treated the man again as before, not minding in the least— such was his moral capacity.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，年四十七。

translations.literal: He died in office at the age of forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 邵雍字堯夫。

translations.literal: Shao Yong, courtesy name Yaofu.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Yong, styled Yaofu.

sentences.zh: 其先范陽人，父古徙衡漳，又徙共城。

translations.literal: His ancestors were from Fanyang; his father Gu moved to Hengzhang, then again to Gongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were from Fanyang; his father Gu moved to Hengzhang, then again to Gongcheng.

sentences.zh: 雍年三十，游河南，葬其親伊水上，遂為河南人。

translations.literal: At thirty Yong traveled to Henan, buried his parents beside the Yi River, and thereafter became a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty Yong traveled to Henan, buried his parents beside the Yi River, and thereafter became a man of Henan.

sentences.zh: 雍少時，自雄其才，慷慨欲樹功名。

translations.literal: In youth Yong was proud of his talent and, full of ardor, wished to establish merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yong was proud of his talent and, full of ardor, wished to establish merit and fame.

sentences.zh: 於書無所不讀，始為學，即堅苦刻厲，寒不爐，暑不扇，夜不就席者數年。

translations.literal: There was no book he did not read; from the moment he undertook serious study he was stern, arduous, and exacting— for years in cold he used no brazier, in heat no fan, and at night did not go to bed.
translations.idiomatic: There was no book he did not read; from the moment he undertook serious study he was stern, arduous, and exacting— for years in cold he used no brazier, in heat no fan, and at night did not go to bed.

sentences.zh: 已而歎曰：「昔人尚友于古，而吾獨未及四方。

translations.literal: After a time he sighed and said: "The ancients sought friendship with the past, yet I alone have not yet reached the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he sighed and said: "The ancients sought friendship with the past, yet I alone have not yet reached the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 」於是逾河、汾，涉淮、漢，周流齊、魯、宋、鄭之墟，久之，幡然來歸，曰：「道在是矣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he crossed the Yellow and Fen rivers, traversed the Huai and Han, and wandered through the ruins of Qi, Lu, Song, and Zheng; after a long while he returned with a change of heart, saying: "The Way is here.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he crossed the Yellow and Fen rivers, traversed the Huai and Han, and wandered through the ruins of Qi, Lu, Song, and Zheng; after a long while he returned with a change of heart, saying: "The Way is here.

sentences.zh: 」遂不復出。

translations.literal: " And never went abroad again.
translations.idiomatic: And never went abroad again.

sentences.zh: 北海李之才攝共城令，聞雍好學，嘗造其廬，謂曰：「子亦聞物理性命之學乎？

translations.literal: Li Zhicai of Beihai, acting magistrate of Gongcheng, heard that Yong loved learning, once visited his cottage and said: "Have you also heard of the learning of natural principles and human nature and fate?
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhicai of Beihai, acting magistrate of Gongcheng, heard that Yong loved learning, once visited his cottage and said: "Have you also heard of the learning of natural principles and human nature and fate?

sentences.zh: 」雍對曰：「幸受教。

translations.literal: " Yong replied: "I would be fortunate to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Yong replied: "I would be fortunate to receive instruction.

sentences.zh: 」乃事之才，受《河圖》、《洛書》、《宓義》八卦六十四卦圖像。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he served Zhicai and received the Hetu, Luoshu, Fuxi's Images of the eight trigrams and sixty-four hexagrams.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he served Zhicai and received the Hetu, Luoshu, and Fuxi's images of the eight trigrams and sixty-four hexagrams.

sentences.zh: 之才之傳，遠有端緒，而雍探賾索隱，妙悟神契，洞徹蘊奧，汪洋浩博，多其所自得者。

translations.literal: Although Zhicai's transmission had a distant beginning, Yong explored the hidden and searched out the obscure, attained wondrous insight through spiritual accord, penetrated to the hidden depths, and was vast and overflowing in breadth; much of what he gained was of his own attainment.
translations.idiomatic: Although Zhicai's transmission had a distant beginning, Yong explored the hidden and searched out the obscure, attained wondrous insight through spiritual accord, penetrated to the hidden depths, and was vast and overflowing in breadth; much of what he gained was of his own attainment.

sentences.zh: 及其學益老，德益邵，玩心高明，以觀夫天地之運化，陰陽之消長，遠而古今世變，微而走飛草木之性情，深造曲暢，庶幾所謂不惑，而非依仿象類、億則屢中者。

translations.literal: As his learning grew ever more mature and his virtue ever more flourishing, he cultivated a lofty and illumined mind to observe Heaven and Earth's transformations, the waxing and waning of yin and yang; far back through the changes of ages past and present, and down to the temperaments of plants, birds, beasts, and insects— he penetrated deeply and expressed it with supple fullness, almost achieving what is called freedom from doubt, and not merely the sort who imitate likenesses and guess repeatedly until they hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: As his learning grew ever more mature and his virtue ever more flourishing, he cultivated a lofty and illumined mind to observe Heaven and Earth's transformations and the waxing and waning of yin and yang; far back through the changes of ages past and present, and down to the temperaments of plants, birds, beasts, and insects— he penetrated deeply and expressed it with supple fullness, almost achieving what is called freedom from doubt, and not merely the sort who imitate likenesses and guess repeatedly until they hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 遂衍宓羲先天之旨，著書十余萬言行於世，然世之知其道者鮮矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he developed Fuxi's doctrine of the Prior Heaven, composed works of more than one hundred thousand characters that circulated in the world— yet those in the age who truly knew his Way were few.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he developed Fuxi's doctrine of the Prior Heaven, composed works of more than one hundred thousand characters that circulated in the world— yet those in the age who truly knew his Way were few.

sentences.zh: 初至洛，蓬蓽環堵，不芘風雨，躬樵爨以事父母，雖平居屢空，而怡然有所甚樂，人莫能窺也。

translations.literal: When he first arrived in Luoyang, his dwelling was a ring of brushwood thatched huts, unable to keep out wind and rain; he himself cut firewood and cooked to serve his parents. Though in ordinary times he was often empty-handed, he was yet cheerful with a deep joy that others could not fathom.
translations.idiomatic: When he first came to Luoyang, he lived in a ring of thatched huts that could not keep out wind and rain; he cut his own firewood and cooked to support his parents. Though he was often penniless in daily life, he remained serenely joyful in a way others could not fathom.

sentences.zh: 及執親喪，哀毀盡禮。

translations.literal: When he undertook mourning for his parents, his grief and devastation fully observed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When he observed mourning for his parents, his grief fully accorded with ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 富弼、司馬光、呂公著諸賢退居洛中，雅敬雍，恒相從遊，為市園宅。

translations.literal: Fu Bi, Sima Guang, Lü Gongzhu, and other worthies who had retired to Luoyang all elegantly respected Yong and constantly accompanied him in outings; they bought him a garden residence in the market district.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi, Sima Guang, Lü Gongzhu, and other eminent men who had retired to Luoyang all held Yong in high regard and often joined him on outings; together they purchased a garden residence for him in the city.

sentences.zh: 雍歲時耕稼，僅給衣食。

translations.literal: Yong farmed each season, barely supplying food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yong farmed through the seasons, barely earning enough for food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 名其居曰「安樂窩」，因自號安樂先生。

translations.literal: He named his dwelling the "Nest of Peace and Joy," and thereby styled himself Master of Peace and Joy.
translations.idiomatic: He named his dwelling the "Nest of Peace and Joy" and took for himself the style Master of Peace and Joy.

sentences.zh: 旦則焚香燕坐，晡時酌酒三四甌，微醺即止，常不及醉也，興至輒哦詩自詠。

translations.literal: In the morning he burned incense and sat at ease; in the late afternoon he poured three or four cups of wine, stopping when slightly tipsy and ordinarily not reaching drunkenness; when inspiration came he would chant poetry to himself.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning he burned incense and sat in quiet meditation; in the late afternoon he would drink three or four cups of wine, stopping at a pleasant glow and rarely becoming drunk; when the mood struck him, he chanted poetry for his own delight.

sentences.zh: 春秋時出遊城中，風雨常不出，出則乘小車，一人挽之，惟意所適。

translations.literal: In spring and autumn he would go out into the city; in wind and rain he ordinarily did not go out. When he went out he rode a small cart with one man drawing it, going wherever his mind wished.
translations.idiomatic: In spring and autumn he would tour the city; in wind and rain he usually stayed home. When he went out, he rode in a small cart drawn by a single attendant, going wherever inclination led him.

sentences.zh: 士大夫家識其車音，爭相迎候，童孺廝隸皆歡相謂曰：「吾家先生至也。

translations.literal: Scholar-official households who recognized the sound of his cart vied to welcome him; children and servants alike joyfully said to one another: "Our family's Master has arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Households of scholar-officials who recognized the sound of his cart competed to welcome him; children and servants alike would exclaim with delight, "Our Master has come!"

sentences.zh: 」不復稱其姓字。

translations.literal: They no longer called him by his surname and given name.
translations.idiomatic: They no longer addressed him by his formal name.

sentences.zh: 或留信宿乃去。

translations.literal: Sometimes they kept him for a night or two before he departed.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes they kept him overnight or for two nights before he moved on.

sentences.zh: 好事者別作屋如雍所居，以候其至，名曰「行窩」。

translations.literal: Enthusiasts separately built houses like Yong's dwelling to await his arrival, naming them "Traveling Nests."
translations.idiomatic: Admirers built houses modeled on his dwelling to await his visits, calling them "Traveling Nests."

sentences.zh: 司馬光兄事雍，而二人純德尤鄉里所慕向，父子昆弟每相飭曰：「毋為不善，恐司馬端明、邵先生知。

translations.literal: Sima Guang treated Yong as an elder brother, and the two men's pure virtue was especially what the neighborhood admired and looked toward; fathers, sons, and brothers would admonish one another: "Do no wrong, lest Sima the Illustrious Ming and Master Shao find out."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang treated Yong with the deference due an elder brother, and the pure virtue of both men was especially admired throughout the neighborhood; fathers, sons, and brothers would warn one another, "Do nothing wrong, lest Sima the Illustrious Ming or Master Shao find out."

sentences.zh: 」士之道洛者，有不之公府，必之雍。

translations.literal: Scholars who came to Luoyang, if they did not visit the government offices, would surely visit Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars arriving in Luoyang, if they did not call at the government offices, were sure to visit Shao Yong.

sentences.zh: 雍德氣粹然，望之知其賢，然不事表襮，不設防畛，群居燕笑終日，不為甚異。

translations.literal: Yong's virtue and bearing were utterly pure; seeing him one knew he was worthy, yet he did not make a display of ornament, set up no barriers, and in group gatherings would laugh and jest all day without being greatly different from others.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's moral bearing was utterly pure; one glance revealed his worthiness, yet he made no show of ornament, set up no barriers between himself and others, and in company would laugh and talk through the day without striking anyone as odd.

sentences.zh: 與人言，樂道其善而隱其惡。

translations.literal: In speaking with people, he delighted in their good points and concealed their faults.
translations.idiomatic: In conversation he delighted in people's virtues and concealed their faults.

sentences.zh: 有就問學則答之，未嘗強以語人。

translations.literal: If someone came to ask about learning he answered; he never forced his words on others.
translations.idiomatic: When someone came to inquire about learning, he answered; he never pressed his views on others uninvited.

sentences.zh: 人無貴賤少長，一接以誠，故賢者悅其德，不賢者服其化。

translations.literal: Whether person was noble or base, young or old, he received all with sincerity; therefore the worthy rejoiced in his virtue, and even the unworthy were transformed by his influence.
translations.idiomatic: Whether high or low, young or old, he received everyone with sincerity; the worthy rejoiced in his virtue, and even the unworthy were swayed by his influence.

sentences.zh: 一時洛中人才特盛，而忠厚之風聞天下。

translations.literal: For a time talent in Luoyang was especially flourishing, and the ethos of honest generosity was heard throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: For a time talent in Luoyang flourished as never before, and a spirit of honest generosity was renowned throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 熙寧行新法，吏牽迫不可為，或投劾去。

translations.literal: When the Xining new laws were implemented, officials were driven and constrained until they could not act, and some submitted their resignations and left.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xining reforms were implemented, officials were so harassed and constrained that some resigned their posts and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 雍門生故友居州縣者，皆貽書訪雍，雍曰：「此賢者所當盡力之時，新法固嚴，能寬一分，則民受一分賜矣。

translations.literal: Yong's students and old friends serving in prefectures and counties all sent letters asking Yong; Yong said: "This is the time when the worthy ought to exert their utmost effort. The new laws are indeed strict, but if one can loosen them by a single degree, the people receive a single degree of grace."
translations.idiomatic: Former students and friends serving in the provinces all wrote to consult Yong. He replied, "This is the time when men of worth should do their utmost. The new laws are indeed harsh, but if you can soften them by even one degree, the people gain one degree of relief."

sentences.zh: 投劾何益耶？」

translations.literal: What use is submitting one's resignation?"
translations.idiomatic: What good does resignation do?"

sentences.zh: 嘉祐詔求遺逸，留守王拱辰以雍應詔，授將作監主簿，復舉逸士，補潁州團練推官，皆固辭乃受命，竟稱疾不之官。

translations.literal: In the Jiayou era an edict sought men of hidden worth; the Luoyang intendant Wang Gongchen recommended Yong in response; he was appointed Master of Works clerk, then again recommended as a recluse of outstanding talent and supplemented as militia push-officer of Yingzhou—all firmly declined before accepting appointment, yet in the end cited illness and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiayou era, when the throne sought men of hidden talent, Luoyang Intendant Wang Gongchen recommended Yong; he was appointed clerk in the Directorate of Works, then recommended again as an outstanding recluse and offered the post of militia push-officer in Yingzhou—each time he firmly declined before accepting, yet in the end cited illness and never took office.

sentences.zh: 熙寧十年，卒，年六十七，贈秘書省著作郎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xining he died, aged sixty-seven, and was posthumously granted Secretary Director of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xining he died at the age of sixty-seven and was posthumously granted the title Director of Works in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元祐中賜諡康節。

translations.literal: In the Yuanyou era he was granted the posthumous title Lord Kangjie.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanyou era he was granted the posthumous title Lord Kangjie.

sentences.zh: 雍高明英邁，迥出千古，而坦夷渾厚，不見圭角，是以清而不激，和而不流，人與交久，益尊信之。

translations.literal: Yong was lofty, bright, and far-ranging, transcending a thousand ages, yet level and thickly honest, showing no sharp corners; therefore he was clear without being cutting, harmonious without being drifting; the longer people associated with him, the more they honored and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Yong was brilliant and far-seeing, transcending his age, yet plain and warmly honest, without a sharp edge; he was clear without being harsh, harmonious without being unprincipled; the longer people knew him, the more they honored and trusted him.

sentences.zh: 河南程顥初侍其父識雍，論議終日，退而歎曰：「堯夫，內聖外王之學也。」

translations.literal: Cheng Hao of Henan, when he first attended his father in meeting Yong, discoursed with him all day; on returning he sighed and said: "Yaofu—this is learning of inner sagehood and outer kingliness."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hao of Henan, when he first accompanied his father to meet Yong, talked with him all day; on returning he sighed and said, "Yaofu possesses the learning of inner sagehood and outer kingliness."

sentences.zh: 雍知慮絕人，遇事能前知。

translations.literal: Yong's knowledge and deliberation surpassed others; when matters arose he could know them beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's insight surpassed that of ordinary men; when events arose he could foresee them.

sentences.zh: 程頤嘗曰：「其心虛明，自能知之。

translations.literal: Cheng Yi once said: "His mind is empty and bright and thereby knows of itself."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi once said, "His mind is empty and luminous, and thereby knows of itself."

sentences.zh: 」當時學者因雍超詣之識，務高雍所為，至謂雍有玩世之意；

translations.literal: Scholars of the time, because Yong's foreknowledge exceeded ordinary understanding, exalted what Yong did, even saying Yong had the air of treating the world as a game;
translations.idiomatic: Scholars of the day, because Yong's foresight exceeded ordinary understanding, exalted his ways, even claiming that he treated the world as a mere game;

sentences.zh: 又因雍之前知，謂雍於凡物聲氣之所感觸，輒以其動而推其變焉。

translations.literal: and because of Yong's prior knowledge, said that whenever ordinary things' sounds and qi were touched and stirred, he would take their movement and infer their transformation.
translations.idiomatic: and because of his reputation for foreknowledge, held that whenever any object's sounds or vital forces were stirred, he would read their movement and infer what change would follow.

sentences.zh: 於是摭世事之已然者，皆以雍言先之，雍蓋未必然也。

translations.literal: Thereupon they gathered matters of the world that had already happened and all said Yong had spoken of them first—yet Yong was probably not really so.
translations.idiomatic: They then collected events that had already occurred and declared that Yong had predicted them all beforehand—though in fact he had probably done nothing of the kind.

sentences.zh: 雍疾病，司馬光、張載、程顥、程頤晨夕候之，將終，共議喪葬事外庭，雍皆能聞眾人所言，召子伯溫謂曰：「諸君欲葬我近城地，當從先塋爾。

translations.literal: When Yong was ill, Sima Guang, Zhang Zai, Cheng Hao, and Cheng Yi attended him morning and evening; as he was about to die, they together discussed funeral arrangements in the outer courtyard. Yong could hear everything the assembly said; he summoned his son Bowen and said: "The gentlemen wish to bury me on land near the city—you should follow the ancestral graves."
translations.idiomatic: When Yong fell ill, Sima Guang, Zhang Zai, Cheng Hao, and Cheng Yi attended him morning and night. As death approached, they discussed funeral arrangements in the outer courtyard; Yong could hear everything they said. He summoned his son Bowen and said, "Your friends wish to bury me near the city—you should place me with the ancestral graves instead."

sentences.zh: 」既葬，顥為銘墓，稱雍之道純一不雜，就其所至，可謂安且成矣。

translations.literal: After the burial, Hao composed the tomb inscription, praising that Yong's Way was pure and undivided; as far as he reached, one may call it peaceful and accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial, Cheng Hao composed the tomb inscription, praising Yong's Way as pure and undivided; in what he attained, one may say he achieved peace and completion.

sentences.zh: 所著書曰《皇極經世》、《觀物內外篇》、《漁樵問對》，詩曰《伊川擊壤集》。

translations.literal: Books he authored include Supreme Pole Governing the Age, Inner and Outer Chapters on Observing Things, Dialogues of Fisherman and Woodcutter; his poetry is called the Jichuan Collection of Striking the Earth.
translations.idiomatic: His written works include Supreme Pole Governing the Age, Inner and Outer Chapters on Observing Things, and Dialogues of Fisherman and Woodcutter; his poetry is collected in the Jichuan Striking-the-Earth Collection.

sentences.zh: 子伯溫，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Bowen has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bowen is treated in a separate biography.
